title: Assay project overview
text: Assay project overview Assay is an agent-facing environment for factor research, combining market-data readers, expression evaluation, portfolio backtests, durable research sessions, factor lifecycle records, and inspection tools. External agents choose the model, hypotheses, and research policy; Assay executes and records their experiments. QFinVerse is an optional market-data source, and other backends can be integrated. Research workflow Register a dataset and start or resume a research session. The agent reads prior context, lints and evaluates a candidate, inspects the resulting metrics or failure, and saves its decision or handoff note. Sessions retain experiment IDs, budgets, parent links, and exportable records. Research audit examines those records; it does not prove investment performance or automatically rerun them. The default research evaluator runs in process. The optional factordb_ades backend links an experiment to a FactorDB job executed by ADES workers. A direct FactorDB job is distinct from a research session. A temporary panel session is also distinct from a durable research session and must be recreated after restart. Interfaces and capabilities Area Entry point Agent tools MCP , including dataset, experiment, FactorDB and audit tools Programmatic access REST , Python SDK , CLI Human research Research workbench and WebUI Execution Portfolio backtesting , factor evaluation, data readers Persistence Agent research , FactorDB , session manifests The public service is at https://assay.qfinverse.com/, with MCP at /mcp/ and REST under /v1/ . Check /.well-known/assay.json for the deployed version, tool discovery, authentication, and workspace scope. Personal keys and model provider keys serve different purposes; Assay does not require a model key on the server. The deployment guide explains reviewer access. Version and evidence boundaries The repository working tree and a deployed service can be different versions. At the 2026-11-13 inspection, the public build was 03bab24 and used a shared research workspace. Later local changes include private account workspaces, trailing-liquidity inputs, and idempotent ADES submissions. The changes require an explicit release before they are available on that service. Account-level hard CPU, memory, and storage quotas are not implemented. Dataset configuration hashes do not freeze a physical market-data snapshot. The repository provides automated tests and performance commands . Component timings depend on inputs and execution assumptions and do not establish the performance of a complete autonomous workflow.

title: Getting Started
text: Getting Started Assay scores factor expressions on point-in-time data: IC, RankIC, decay, turnover, redundancy, and a portfolio backtest with costs. There are two ways in: the hosted site, or your own install. Use the hosted site assay.qfinverse.com runs Assay on QFinVerse's US daily data (2003 onward, universes TOP500 / TOP1000 / TOP3000, SP500, NASDAQ100). See US data from QFinVerse for what that data holds. Get an invitation. Sign-up is by invitation only. Ask an admin for a link, open it, and choose a username and password (at least 10 characters). Sign in at /login . The session lasts 7 days. Score a factor. Open Single Factor Test , pick a universe and period in the bar at the top, write an expression such as -ts_delta(close, 5) / ts_delay(close, 5) and press Evaluate . Save good ones to the library. See the WebUI guide . Create an API key for scripts and agents: Account → API keys → Create key . The key ( asy_... ) is shown once. It acts as you; revoke it when you no longer need it. Call the REST API with the key in the X-API-Key header: export ASSAY_KEY=asy_... curl -s -X POST https://assay.qfinverse.com/v1/factor/evaluate \ -H "X-API-Key: $ASSAY_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"expr": "-ts_delta(close, 5) / ts_delay(close, 5)", "universe": "SP500", "period": ["2019-01-01", "2026-10-30"], "horizons": [1, 5, 10, 20]}' All endpoints are listed in the REST guide ; the interactive schema is at /docs on the site. Run it yourself 1. Install From source (there is no PyPI release): git clone https://github.com/QFinVerse/Assay.git && cd Assay pip install -e ".[perf,api,mcp]" # perf = numba + scipy (much faster evaluation) Without installing, everything also runs with PYTHONPATH=src . 2. Point it at data Settings are environment variables, read by AssayConfig.from_env() . A .env file in the project is loaded at import; the shell always wins. See .env.example . US, from a QFinVerse daily panel (recommended): set ASSAY_QFV_PANEL_DIR to the panel root. Nothing else to ingest; see US data from QFinVerse . US, from a local MASSIVE mirror : set MASSIVE_DATA_DIR and build the Parquet stores: export MASSIVE_DATA_DIR=/data/massive_data # local mirror, no credentials needed export ASSAY_DATA_DIR=data # where the stores are written python -m assay.cli prepare-nasdaq100 --start 2025-01-01 --end 2026-06-09 python -m assay.cli status China A-shares and Hong Kong come from Tushare; see Multi-market and Tushare . The MASSIVE day bars are OHLCV plus trade count; there is no vwap field. 3. Evaluate a factor From the CLI: python -m assay.cli parse 'cs_rank(ts_corr(close, volume, 20))' # syntax only, no data python -m assay.cli run 'cs_rank(ts_corr(close, volume, 20))' \ --start 2025-01-02 --end 2026-06-09 From Python ( SDK guide ): import assay report = assay.backtest( "cs_rank(ts_corr(close, volume, 20))", universe="NASDAQ100", period=("2025-01-02", "2026-06-09"), ) print(report.rank_ic, report.rank_icir, report.decay_halflife_days, report.failure_mode) A FactorReport holds ic / rank_ic / icir / rank_icir , ic_by_horizon , decay, turnover, redundancy, look-ahead checks, a suggestion and structured diagnostics . .to_dict() is JSON-safe. 4. Backtest a portfolio from assay.portfolio import PortfolioBacktestConfig cfg = PortfolioBacktestConfig(universe="NASDAQ100", period_start="2025-01-02", period_end="2026-06-09", rebalance_type="monthly", weight_method="signal_prop") pf = assay.backtest_portfolio("cs_rank(ts_returns(close, 20))", cfg) print(pf.sharpe, pf.max_drawdown, pf.annual_turnover, pf.cost_drag) See the portfolio backtest guide . 5. Start the server python -m assay.cli serve-api --port 8000 # REST API, WebUI and Doc Hub on :8000 python -m assay.cli serve-mcp # MCP server over stdio, for agents The server is open by default. To require sign-in, set ASSAY_ACCOUNTS=1 and create the first admin with the token in the state directory; see REST API → Auth . Where to go next Guide What it covers WebUI the console: pages, controls, accounts US data from QFinVerse universes, security ids, splits and dividends Data & Adjustment how prices are adjusted and read point-in-time Data pipeline MASSIVE loaders, prepare-nasdaq100 , data folders Python SDK backtest , Session , batch_backtest , library , backtest_portfolio CLI every python -m assay.cli subcommand REST API /v1/* and /auth/* endpoints, SSE streaming, auth modes MCP server agent tools and client setup Portfolio backtest config, running, metrics, A-share notes Performance the Alpha-101 cache benchmark

title: WebUI
text: WebUI The console is served by the API server itself: no install, no build step. The code is in src/assay/api/static/ ; the design notes are in the WebUI design doc . python -m assay.cli serve-api --port 8000 # then open http://localhost:8000 On assay.qfinverse.com you sign in first; see Accounts below. Layout Sidebar. Pages in three groups (Research, Data, Admin), then QFinVerse, theme, language, your account and Collapse . Docs opens the Doc Hub in a new tab. The bottom line shows the running build. Context bar. Universe and period apply to every page. The pill on the right shows how far the data goes; amber or red means stale or unreachable. Theme (system, light, dark) is shared with QFinVerse. Charts redraw after a switch. Pages Dashboard. Data status, four KPI cards, the factor leaderboard (sort, minimum ICIR, source, hide redundant), the top factors and a calendar of trading days with data. Single Factor Test. Write an expression in qlib or Python syntax; it is checked as you type and the parse tree is one click away. Evaluate (or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter) streams the results: IC and RankIC over time, decay by horizon, quintile returns, IC by month, turnover, and a summary with a suggestion. Save puts the report in the library; Portfolio backtest opens the next step with the same factor. Factor Library. Every saved factor, with search and filters. Tabs: factor detail, correlation matrix (with a prune preview), alpha-space map, IC heatmap and lineage. Factor Combination. Pick factors, choose a method (equal weight, IC-weighted, linear and tree models where installed) and score the composite on train, validation and test periods. Runs can be saved and reloaded. Portfolio Backtest. Turns a factor into a long or long-short book with rebalancing, weights, limits and costs, and reports NAV, Sharpe, drawdown, turnover and cost drag. Chart. Daily bars for one symbol, with the adjustment mode and a factor overlay. Data Manager (admins). Sources, ingest jobs, schedules and the cache. On a server that reads US data from QFinVerse, US needs no jobs here. Accounts When the server runs with accounts ( ASSAY_ACCOUNTS=1 , as on assay.qfinverse.com): Sign-up is by invitation. Open the link an admin sent, pick a username and a password of at least 10 characters. Account (click your name in the sidebar): change your name and password, and manage API keys. A new key is shown once; send it as X-API-Key from scripts and agents. Users (admins): create invitations (role, number of uses, days valid), change roles, disable or delete accounts, and issue one-time password reset links. Tips An evaluation needs data for the whole window: a 20-day factor needs 20 days of history before the first date, or it comes back empty with an ALL_NAN diagnostic. After a deployment, a reload picks up the new build (assets are revalidated on every load). The live agent feed on the Dashboard is not wired yet; the right column shows the top factors instead.

title: CLI Reference
text: CLI Reference All commands run as python -m assay.cli <subcommand> (or assay <subcommand> once pip install -e . 'd — the console scripts are assay and assay-data ). Commands resolve config from the environment / .env ; only data-touching commands need MASSIVE credentials. Data pipeline Command Purpose discover List MASSIVE flat-file prefixes (connectivity sanity check) prepare-nasdaq100 --start S --end E Full prepare: universe → corp-actions → prices. Flags: --skip-universe/-corp-actions/-prices universe --index NASDAQ100 --start S --end E Build universe_snapshots corp-actions --start S --end E [--symbols A,B] Fetch splits & dividends prices --start S --end E [--symbols A,B] Download & normalize day aggregates status Show ingested rows, date range, partitions verify --start S --end E [--adj split] Read a PIT panel and print a summary Factor engine Command Purpose parse '<expr>' Parse a factor expression → dialect, AST, fields, operators (no data needed) eval '<expr>' --start S --end E [--as-of D] [--adj split] [--index NASDAQ100] Evaluate the factor matrix over the PIT panel; print coverage + top/bottom names Backtest & library (SDK-backed) Command Purpose run '<expr>' --start S --end E [...] Full scored FactorReport summary (rank_ic, rank_icir, decay, failure_mode, suggestion) `batch <file exprs...> --start S --end E [--output results.parquet]` report <factor_id> Pretty-print a saved factor from the library library list/get/delete/prune [...] Manage the factor library (e.g. library list --sort rank_icir --limit 20 ) portfolio '<expr>' --start S --end E [--rebalance monthly] [--weight-method signal_prop] [--market US] [--long-short] [--output pf.json] Run a portfolio backtest; print total/annual return, Sharpe, max drawdown, turnover, cost drag Servers Command Purpose serve-api [--host 0.0.0.0] [--port 8000] Run the FastAPI REST API + WebUI (uvicorn) `serve-mcp [--transport stdio http Examples # prepare + inspect python -m assay.cli prepare-nasdaq100 --start 2025-01-01 --end 2026-06-09 python -m assay.cli status # evaluate python -m assay.cli parse 'cs_rank(ts_corr(close, volume, 20))' python -m assay.cli run 'cs_rank(ts_corr(close, volume, 20))' --start 2025-01-02 --end 2026-06-09 # batch from a file printf 'ts_returns(close, 20)\nts_corr(close, volume, 20)\n' > factors.txt python -m assay.cli batch factors.txt --start 2025-01-02 --end 2026-06-09 --output out.parquet # portfolio python -m assay.cli portfolio 'cs_rank(ts_returns(close, 20))' \ --start 2025-01-02 --end 2026-06-09 --rebalance monthly --weight-method signal_prop # serve python -m assay.cli serve-api --port 8000 # http://localhost:8000 Add -v before any subcommand for debug logging.

title: Deploying Assay
text: Deploying Assay The public base URL is https://assay.qfinverse.com . REST and MCP run in the same API process, use the same authentication and share persistent research state. Interface Public endpoint Web workbench https://assay.qfinverse.com/ Streamable HTTP MCP https://assay.qfinverse.com/mcp/ Research REST https://assay.qfinverse.com/v1/research OpenAPI / interactive API https://assay.qfinverse.com/openapi.json / /docs Connection discovery https://assay.qfinverse.com/.well-known/assay.json Documentation https://assay.qfinverse.com/doc/ Liveness / authenticated readiness /health / /ready The discovery document is Assay-specific metadata. It advertises the interface version, actual tool count/schema digest and authentication methods. It is not an OAuth discovery document. Remote clients need support for a Bearer token or X-API-Key ; clients that require OAuth-only servers need an additional integration. Install and configure Python 3.12 and the versions in deploy/constraints.txt are used by the deployment acceptance tests. From the release checkout: python3.12 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install -c deploy/constraints.txt '.[api,mcp,perf]' python scripts/build_doc_hub.py Run the document build with the development interpreter that has markdown-it-py , or ship the already generated static documentation. It is not a runtime dependency. Use deploy/assay.env.example for the environment, assay.service for systemd, and Caddyfile for TLS and streaming proxying. The templates assume a dedicated assay user, the checkout/venv at /opt/assay , configuration at /etc/assay/assay.env , writable local storage at /var/lib/assay and prepared, read-only US data at /srv/assay/market/us . Create the directories and assign the runtime directory to that user before starting the unit. Adjust paths to the host. Key settings: ASSAY_DEPLOYMENT=production ASSAY_PUBLIC_URL=https://assay.qfinverse.com ASSAY_MCP_HTTP=1 ASSAY_ACCOUNTS=1 ASSAY_CORS_ORIGINS=https://assay.qfinverse.com ASSAY_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/assay ASSAY_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/assay/accounts ASSAY_CONFIG_FILE=/var/lib/assay/config.json ASSAY_DATA_DIR_US=/srv/assay/market/us Production mode rejects a missing HTTPS public origin, missing authentication or disabled/unavailable MCP. Configure ASSAY_PUBLIC_URL as an origin with no path, query or embedded credential. The public URL is used in discovery and OpenAPI; proxy-provided Host values cannot replace it. When using accounts for a new installation, visit /login , then use the first-setup token from ASSAY_STATE_DIR/setup_token to create the administrator. Existing installations retain their auth database and secret. Researchers join by invitation and create a personal API key on the Account page. The server needs no LLM key; the external agent supplies its own model connection. Start with one API worker. Research SQLite state is persistent, while temporary panel sessions and cache counters are process-local. The in-process data scheduler also runs per process. Stateless MCP HTTP does not make these components distributed. For FactorDB/ADES, additionally configure its writable registry/queue directory, the read-only QFV panel and worker-only keys; the base template does not enable it. For existing multi-market deployments, retain ASSAY_DATA_DIR_CN and ASSAY_DATA_DIR_HK with their SNAPSHOT.json , and verify per-market versions at /v1/fdb/markets . Updated workers advertise all available panels and info.lease_token_supported=true . During a rolling upgrade, legacy workers can continue ordinary compute jobs; token-fenced research tasks are leased only to workers supporting that protocol. Upgrade the controller first, followed by at least one worker supporting the target market. Corrected next_close and newly supported close jobs also require upgraded workers; legacy workers continue ordinary next_open jobs. The next_close forward-return cache uses a separate v2 filename so pre-upgrade labels cannot be reused. Reverse proxy and transport Preserve the external Host , Authorization , X-API-Key , Accept and MCP protocol headers. Disable response buffering for /mcp/ and evaluation streams. Caddy's template flushes immediately; for nginx use proxy_buffering off , HTTP/1.1 and a read timeout long enough for a complete experiment. Trust forwarded headers only from the actual proxy, as the systemd command does for loopback. Use /mcp/ as the canonical client URL. /mcp returns a relative 308 redirect. The MCP transport validates Host and Origin against the configured endpoint and allowed browser origins, including equivalent explicit default ports. CORS exposes the MCP session/protocol headers. Legacy SSE is restricted to local use; the public endpoint uses Streamable HTTP and the installed SDK's negotiated protocol version. Verify the release Set ASSAY_MCP_API_KEY through your normal secret manager or shell, then run: PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/check_deployment.py \ --base-url https://assay.qfinverse.com \ --output artifacts/deployment-release/check.json The checker reads health, discovery and OpenAPI; verifies unauthenticated rejection; checks authenticated readiness and dataset access; initializes a real MCP session; and calls tool discovery, lint and dataset listing. It creates no dataset, session or experiment and makes no model calls. No key is written to its report. A missing key yields an incomplete result and exit code 2, rather than a successful verdict. /health is cheap process liveness. /ready verifies that the research database can enter a write transaction and the MCP transport is available; it requires the same credentials as REST. It does not certify market coverage. Before admitting a mining job, separately check backend availability, its requested data/calendar window and a small authorized factor experiment against the prepared data. Lint alone does not exercise factor execution or portfolio accounting. Before switching traffic, run the regression suite and verify a new authenticated research session through MCP and REST. Preserve its request ID and confirm the same attempt after restart. The tests in tests/api/test_deployment.py exercise real TCP MCP connections; existing research transport tests cover restart, budgets and migration. Persistent state and release boundaries Back up /var/lib/assay , including research and account databases, auth_secret , configuration and the factor library. Cache files may be rebuilt. Use SQLite's backup API or a stopped service for database copies; copying a live database file alone is not a consistent backup. Keep a protected pre-upgrade snapshot and restore it with the previous release when rolling back across schema changes. When account authentication is enabled, personal accounts use private research, library, combination and FactorDB registries. Service keys continue to use the original shared workspace. Back up the account database and account directories together; existing browser sessions must sign in again after the workspace-identity migration. ADES workers are trusted with the expressions they execute. Temporary panel sessions remain process-local, and account-level CPU, memory and storage hard quotas are not yet enforced; use separate instances when those boundaries are needed. The read-only market-data/atomic-publication contract for compute reuse is described in performance . Full experiment results can be large; use compact research context and the paginated experiment/history endpoints for routine agent reads. Client examples: MCP , reference agent , REST .

title: US data from QFinVerse
text: US data from QFinVerse On assay.qfinverse.com, US universes read the daily panel store that QFinVerse builds from MASSIVE: end-of-day bars from September 2003, splits and dividends, and the MASSIVE ticker reference. Assay does not ingest US data itself in this setup. Setup export ASSAY_QFV_PANEL_DIR=/srv/qfinverse/data/daily_panel # the store's root (holds CURRENT) assay serve-api The reader is vendored in src/assay/data/qfv_panel (format qfv-daily-panel/1 ); scripts/sync_qfv_panel.py copies it again from a QFinVerse checkout. QFinVerse updates the store every trading day at 21:45 New York time; Assay switches to the new version on its next request, and results cached for the old version are not reused. Universes Universe Members TOP500 , TOP1000 , TOP3000 most liquid common stocks on the first trading day of each month SP500 , NASDAQ100 dated index histories, matched to QFinVerse securities The TOP universes rank by median dollar volume over the previous 63 trading days (at least 50 days traded, last close at least $5). ETFs, ADRs, preferreds, warrants, units and rights are left out. Membership uses only earlier data and keeps securities that later delisted. An evaluation covers every security that was a member at any time in the period and scores it only on the days it was a member. A universe read from the members on the last day would leave out every stock that dropped out; on NASDAQ100 over 2016–2026 that flips the sign of low-volatility and range factors. Securities Bars carry tickers only, so each security has a permanent id: a ticker that comes back after more than 63 trading days without a bar is a new security; the older one is labelled TICKER~YYYY-MM (for example ABC~2004-03 ); renames are one security when the MASSIVE ticker history or a shared composite FIGI says so ( FB → META ), or when a delisted and a new common stock share a CIK and the price carries on within 25% ( COH → TPR ). A ticker in an expression or a chart means the security that held it on the last day of the window. Corporate actions Prices are stored as traded and adjusted when read, onto the share basis of the last day of the window. Only events with an ex-date inside the window are applied, so a backtest that ends in the past never sees a later split. Field Meaning open high low close split- and dividend-adjusted (total return basis) volume split-adjusted transactions as reported dvol close × volume, as traded ret daily total return, the same in every window Every split is checked against the prices before it is used: Status Meaning Applied ok prices jump by the split ratio on the ex-date yes moved the jump is a few days off the vendor's date; the split moves there yes no_jump no such jump within 10 trading days: already adjusted, or never happened no small ratio within 10% of 1:1 (stock dividends) yes Dividends are applied as 1 − cash / previous close . A dividend is skipped when it is not paid in USD, when it is more than half the price (nearly always a unit error), or when there is no close in the 15 days before the ex-date. Speed Panels are dense float32 arrays by year, memory-mapped. TOP500 over 2016–2026 loads in about 0.3 s and all of TOP3000 over 2010–2026 in about 3 s. Six factors on SP500 over ten years evaluate in about 11 s, against 54 s on the per-ticker parquet store.

title: Data & Adjustment
headings: 3. How factors see prices under splits & dividends
text: Data & Adjustment This is the most important document for trusting a backtest: what data Assay stores, and exactly what prices a factor sees under corporate actions (splits, dividends). Get this wrong and every IC number is meaningless. Assay's design goal is that a factor can never see information that was not knowable on the query date, and that adjusted prices are reproducible from first principles. 1. Two layers: RAW → ASSAY Layer What Where RAW Vendor data, as delivered, read in place MASSIVE_DATA_DIR (US), TUSHARE_DATA_DIR (CN) ASSAY Normalized, point-in-time parquet stores the engine reads ASSAY_DATA_DIR / ASSAY_DATA_DIR_CN The ingest step ( prepare_us / prepare_cn ) normalizes RAW into a fixed schema and writes the ASSAY stores. Nothing downstream ever reads RAW again — the engine, IC evaluation, portfolio backtest and WebUI all read the ASSAY stores through one interface, DataStore . The ASSAY stores Store Grain Key columns price_raw one row per (date, symbol) date, symbol, open, high, low, close, volume, transactions, as_of_date, source_id adj_events one row per corporate action symbol, ex_date, event_type, split_ratio, dividend_cash, as_of_date, provider_adj_factor universe_snapshots one row per membership change index_id, effective_date, symbols[], as_of_date trade_status (CN) one row per (date, symbol) date, symbol, up_limit, down_limit, limit_up_locked, limit_down_locked, close security_groups (CN) one row per symbol symbol, group, as_of_date Prices are stored raw / unadjusted . Corporate actions live separately in adj_events , and adjustment is applied at read time — never baked into storage. This is what makes any point-in-time slice reproducible: the same raw prices + only the events known as-of a date yield exactly one adjusted panel. 2. Bi-temporal: date vs as_of_date Every stored row carries two times: date — event time : the day the bar/action happened. as_of_date — knowledge time : the first day that row was knowable. Every read takes a required as_of_date , and the store returns only rows with as_of_date <= as_of_date . Look-ahead bias is therefore structurally impossible — you cannot query data that did not yet exist. Knowledge time per source: Source as_of_date is… Price bar (EOD) the trading date (known at that day's close) Split / share change the ex / execution date Cash dividend the declaration date (falls back to ex-date) Universe membership the effective date panel = store.get_panel( fields=["close", "volume"], symbols=universe, start_date="2024-01-01", end_date="2024-06-28", as_of_date="2024-06-28", # REQUIRED — everything after this is invisible adj="split", ) 3. How factors see prices under splits & dividends A factor never touches adj_events directly. It sees the (T, N) price matrices that DataStore.get_panel(..., adj=...) returns, already adjusted. The math lives in adjust.py and is forward (a.k.a. "backward- adjusted to today") : history is rescaled onto the most recent date's basis , so the latest bar always equals the raw price and only the past is rescaled. 3.1 Splits & share changes A share-change event (split, reverse-split, merger ratio) with forward ratio r = split_to / split_from # 2-for-1 split → r = 2 ; 1-for-10 reverse → r = 0.1 divides every price strictly before its ex-date by r , and multiplies the corresponding volume by r . The ex-date bar itself already reflects the split, so it is left unchanged. Multiple splits compose multiplicatively. Reverse splits ( r < 1 ) and merger share-changes use the same mechanism. Example: a 2-for-1 split on 2024-06-10. A close of $400 on 2024-06-07 becomes $200 after adjustment (÷2), lining up continuously with the ~ $200 bars from 2024-06-10 on. Volume on 2024-06-07 is doubled. Returns computed across the split are therefore correct. 3.2 Cash dividends ( adj="total" only) In total mode, a cash dividend D with ex-date e multiplies every price strictly before e by ratio = 1 − D / close_prev where close_prev is the raw close on the session immediately before e . Because both D and close_prev are in raw price space, the dividend factor composes correctly with the split factor ( price_factor = split_factor × dividend_factor ). Two guards: Prior-close gap — if the session before e is more than _MAX_PRIOR_GAP_DAYS = 10 calendar days back (a data hole, or outside the loaded lead-in), the dividend is skipped rather than mis-scaled. Dividend ≥ price — if D ≥ close_prev (ratio ≤ 0), the dividend is skipped rather than flipping the sign of history. 3.3 Adjustment modes ( adj ) Mode Splits Dividends Use when none ✗ ✗ you want the literal traded price (e.g. price-limit logic) split (default) ✓ ✗ most alpha research — continuity across splits, no dividend drift total (alias forward ) ✓ ✓ total-return studies; dividends reinvested The provider's own historical_adjustment_factor is stored but not used for the math — adjustment is computed only from events known as-of the query date, so there is no leakage from a vendor factor that silently encodes future actions. 3.4 Choosing adj for a factor Momentum / reversal / most price-shape factors → split (the default). You want a continuous series without dividend step-downs, but you do not want raw price jumps at splits. Anything comparing to a total-return benchmark, or explicitly modelling reinvested dividends → total . Execution-constraint / limit-up-down logic (CN) → none on the price you compare to the raw up_limit / down_limit bands (see §4). 4. China A-share specifics CN data (Tushare) adds a few wrinkles the US path does not have: 送转 (bonus/transfer shares) are converted to a split ratio: "10转15" → 1 + 15/10 = 2.5 , i.e. treated as a share-change event with r = 2.5 . Cash dividends flow into adj_events.dividend_cash (tax-inclusive value preferred). Price limits (涨跌停) are stored in trade_status ( up_limit / down_limit and the *_locked flags). Use them with adj="none" prices for execution constraints — a name locked limit-up cannot be bought at the close. Volume units — the current Tushare CN ingester stores vol as 100-share lots; it does not convert to shares. Other data sources may use shares. Confirm the source and set the appropriate liquidity volume multiplier when backtesting. Incremental updates fetch by trade-date (all symbols per API call) and append to the per-symbol raw files, so a daily update is a handful of calls, not one per symbol. 5. Reproduce it yourself from assay.data.store import DataStore store = DataStore(cfg) raw = store.get_panel(["close"], syms, s, e, as_of, adj="none") # traded price split = store.get_panel(["close"], syms, s, e, as_of, adj="split") # split-continuous total = store.get_panel(["close"], syms, s, e, as_of, adj="total") # + dividends # The latest bar is identical across modes; only history is rescaled. CLI cross-check (adjusted vs raw around a known action): python -m assay.cli verify --start 2024-06-01 --end 2024-06-30 --adj split See also: Data Pipeline (how to load/update data) · Getting Started · Engineering design .

title: Data Pipeline
text: Data Pipeline Assay transforms a local mirror of the MASSIVE US-equity dataset into point-in-time parquet stores. Nothing is downloaded — the pipeline reads pre-downloaded files from disk. The data layer is the correctness foundation: every read takes an explicit as_of_date , so look-ahead bias is structurally impossible. When ASSAY_QFV_PANEL_DIR is set (as on assay.qfinverse.com), US universes read the QFinVerse daily panel instead and this pipeline is not needed for US data. See US data from QFinVerse . A-share and Hong Kong data still come from Tushare . Local source MASSIVE_DATA_DIR (default /data/massive_data ) is the root of the local mirror, produced out-of-band by the downloader_* scripts. Expected layout: $MASSIVE_DATA_DIR/ ├── us_stocks_sip/day_aggs_v1/{YYYY}/{MM}/{YYYY-MM-DD}.parquet # daily OHLCV bars ├── corporate_actions/splits/{TICKER}.jsonl # one split record per line └── corporate_actions/dividends/{TICKER}.jsonl # one dividend record per line Each day-aggregate parquet has the MASSIVE flat-file columns ticker, volume, open, close, high, low, window_start, transactions ( window_start is the Unix-nanosecond start of the trading-day window in US/Eastern). Stores Under ASSAY_DATA_DIR (default data/ ): <data_dir>/ ├── price_raw/market=US/year=YYYY/month=MM/price_raw.parquet # unadjusted OHLCV + transactions ├── adj_events/market=US/adj_events.parquet # splits & dividends (corp actions) └── universe_snapshots/market=US/universe_snapshots.parquet # PIT index membership The MASSIVE day-aggregate source provides open/high/low/close/volume/transactions — there is no vwap , and market_cap is not ingested. One-shot prepare python -m assay.cli prepare-nasdaq100 --start 2025-01-01 --end 2026-06-09 Runs three stages in order, into the configured data dir: universe — NASDAQ-100 PIT constituent snapshots (the survivorship-bias-free union of every ticker that was a member at any point in the range; built from vendored YAML, no source files needed). corp-actions — splits & dividends read from the local corporate_actions/ JSONL files (best-effort: a failure here no longer aborts the price transfer). prices — daily OHLCV from the local day-aggregate parquet, filtered to the universe, written as monthly partitions. Flags: --skip-universe , --skip-corp-actions , --skip-prices . Data Manager (WebUI / API) The WebUI Data tab (and the /v1/admin/* API) drives the whole data layer without the CLI: Keys & Dirs — configure the MASSIVE S3 credentials (US), the Tushare token + API endpoint (CN/HK), and the data dirs; Test connection lists the datasets your S3 key can read / validates the token. Secrets are stored masked in a git-ignored .assay.config.json . Data Setup — run jobs per market with mode : init — full history (download + ingest); update — incremental download + ingest (CN and HK fetch by trade-date , all symbols per call, so a daily refresh is a handful of API calls, then appends to the raw files); ingest — RAW→ASSAY only , no download (when the raw mirror is already populated). An auto-update schedule (per market, a daily time) queues update jobs automatically. Data Status — per-market cards showing both RAW (source: latest date, size, dir) and ASSAY (store: latest date, trading days, size, dir), plus days-behind and in-sync. Jobs run one-at-a-time in the background with a live progress bar and log. For adjustment semantics (splits/dividends, point-in-time), see Data & Adjustment ( 中文 ). Individual stages python -m assay.cli universe --index NASDAQ100 --start 2025-01-01 --end 2026-06-09 python -m assay.cli corp-actions --start 2025-01-01 --end 2026-06-09 python -m assay.cli prices --start 2025-01-01 --end 2026-06-09 python -m assay.cli discover # show the local source layout (sanity check) Inspect & verify python -m assay.cli status # row counts, date range, partitions python -m assay.cli verify --start 2025-06-01 --end 2025-06-30 --adj split # read a PIT panel --adj is none | split | total (alias forward ). Adjustment uses only corporate actions known as-of the query date. Separate data folders ASSAY_DATA_DIR selects the active store, so you can keep multiple datasets side by side and the loader/engine set up a fresh folder automatically: ASSAY_DATA_DIR=data_2025_2026h1 python -m assay.cli prepare-nasdaq100 --start 2025-01-01 --end 2026-06-09 ASSAY_DATA_DIR=data_2025_2026h1 python -m assay.cli serve-api # engine uses that folder Set it permanently in .env ( ASSAY_DATA_DIR=data_2025_2026h1 ). Folders matching data*/ are git-ignored. Known data caveats No adj_events ⇒ unadjusted splits. If the corp-actions stage was skipped or the local corporate_actions/ tree is missing, the folder has no adj_events , so adj='split' is a no-op and real stock splits appear as large single-day "returns" that pollute factor/portfolio results. Backfill: python -m assay.cli corp-actions --start ... --end ... . vwap is unavailable — factor expressions referencing vwap (and market_cap / cap ) cannot run on ingested data; ~52 of the 101 Alpha-101 factors run on OHLCV alone. See the data-layer design in engineering.md §3.

title: Multi-market support (China A-share + Hong Kong)
headings: 1. Ingest: raw Tushare → canonical CN stores
2. Trading constraints in the portfolio backtest
text: Multi-market support (China A-share + Hong Kong) Assay's data layer and portfolio backtester are market-agnostic: prices, corporate actions and index membership live in canonical stores partitioned by market=... , and the execution simulator already models the A-share microstructure rules. This doc covers running the framework on Chinese A-shares end-to-end, using the Tushare mirror (see tushare.md ). 1. Ingest: raw Tushare → canonical CN stores assay.data.tushare.ingest.prepare_cn reads the raw mirror ( $TUSHARE_DATA_DIR , default /data/tushare_data ) and writes the same canonical stores the US pipeline produces, under market=CN : store source notes price_raw cn/daily unadjusted OHLCV ( volume in 手/lots) adj_events cn/dividend 送转 → forward split_ratio = 1 + stk_div ; pre-tax cash ( cash_div_tax ) → dividend_cash ; only implemented (实施) dividends universe_snapshots cn/index_weight CSI300/500/1000 point-in-time membership (composition-change snapshots) trade_status cn/stk_limit + cn/daily raw 涨停价/跌停价 bands + locked flags (A-share only) security_groups cn/meta/stock_basic per-symbol industry label for sector-neutralisation (current snapshot) # writes market=CN partitions under $ASSAY_DATA_DIR python scripts/prepare_cn.py 2010-01-01 2026-06-27 Adjustment is recomputed from primitive events at read time (the same forward machinery as US equities), so adj="split" adjusts for 送转 only and adj="total" adds cash dividends. 2. Trading constraints in the portfolio backtest The execution layer ( assay.portfolio.execution.ExecutionSimulator ) enforces the A-share rules whenever PortfolioBacktestConfig.market == "A" and the data is present. All three are now wired from the canonical stores: Daily price limits (涨跌停). A buy into a name trading at its ceiling and a sell into one at its floor get zero fill ( blocked_reason limit_up / limit_down ). The backtester auto-loads the real per-board bands from trade_status (10% main board, 20% STAR/ChiNext, 30% BSE, 5% ST) rather than a flat percentage. Limit prices are raw while the price panel is adjusted, so each band is rebased into the panel basis by adj_close / raw_close before the comparison — see PortfolioBacktester._cn_limit_matrices . T+1 settlement. Shares bought on a rebalance cannot be sold the same step ( blocked_reason t_plus_1 ). Active for market == "A" via the preset. Suspension (停牌). A halted name simply has no price_raw bar, so its price is NaN and the executor treats it as untradable ( blocked_reason suspended ). No extra data needed. The A -preset also applies the A-share cost model : 0.05% stamp duty (sell; cut from 0.1% on 2023-08-28), 0.03% commission (min ¥5), 0.002% transfer fee, √-impact k=0.20 . Other market-correctness defaults (preset 'A' ): Long-only enforced. market=='A' with long_short=True raises — A-share 短 selling (融券) is restricted/unavailable, so a short book isn't executable. Total-return basis. The engine's adjustment basis is derived from market (A/HK → total = dividends reinvested, the correct basis for alpha P&L; US → split ), so it never silently aliases two runs in the evaluation cache. Sector-neutralisation uses real industry labels: set sector_neutral=True and the backtester auto-loads security_groups from the store (Tushare industry ); both the signal neutraliser and the sector-weight constraint then engage. Without it, runs are never silently sector-balanced. 3. Running a CN backtest import datetime as dt from assay.config import AssayConfig from assay.data.store.datastore import DataStore from assay.portfolio import PortfolioBacktestConfig, PortfolioBacktester # A CN DataStore reads market=CN partitions; the 'A' preset drives trading rules. store = DataStore(AssayConfig(market="CN", data_dir=AssayConfig.from_env().data_dir)) bt = PortfolioBacktester(store=store) cfg = PortfolioBacktestConfig.preset( "A", universe="CSI300", period_start="2022-01-01", period_end="2023-12-31", rebalance_type="monthly", weight_method="signal_prop", ) report = bt.run("ts_delta(close, 20) / delay(close, 20)", cfg) # a momentum factor print(report.total_return, report.sharpe, report.a_share_metrics) Two market knobs, intentionally separate: AssayConfig.market="CN" selects which data partition the store reads. PortfolioBacktestConfig.market="A" selects the trading-rule regime (limits / T+1 / cost model). report.a_share_metrics reports n_limit_hits , n_forced_holds (T+1), n_blocked_suspended , and the corresponding rates. Universes available for CN: CSI300 , CSI500 , CSI1000 (point-in-time, survivorship-free). 4. Hong Kong HK rides the same canonical stores under market=HK , fed by assay.data.tushare.ingest.prepare_hk (CLI: scripts/prepare_hk.py ). It needs an entitled Tushare endpoint — see tushare.md . store source notes price_raw hk/daily unadjusted OHLCV ( volume in shares , not lots) adj_events hk/adj_factor reconstructed from cum_adjfactor steps, corroborated against pre_close universe_snapshots hk/daily turnover + hk_basic ISIN HK100 and HSHARE100 point-in-time membership trade_status — not written: HKEX has no daily price-limit bands security_groups — not written: Tushare exposes no HK industry classification # writes market=HK partitions under $ASSAY_DATA_DIR_HK (default ./data_hk) python scripts/prepare_hk.py 2015-01-01 2026-07-27 HK100 is the whole-board universe. It ranks every name that actually traded by trailing three-month turnover at each month end and takes the top 100 effective on the next month's first trading day — so a snapshot can never see the returns it would be scored on. HSHARE100 applies exactly the same ranking to H-shares only — mainland-China-incorporated issuers listed on HKEX, as opposed to the red chips (Cayman/Bermuda holding companies) and local Hong Kong issuers that make up the rest of the board. Membership is decided by the ISIN country prefix ( CNE ), which is a property of where the issuer is registered and therefore never changes; because the listings table is downloaded with delisted names included, the pool is survivorship-free. The two universes overlap by roughly half — H-shares that are also among the most-traded names on the board. Use HSHARE100 when the thesis is about mainland corporates (A/H pairs, mainland policy exposure, the Connect flow) and HK100 when it is about the Hong Kong market as a whole. HSI and HSTECH are also registered but are vendored current snapshots and therefore survivorship-biased. The HK preset differs from A in every respect that matters: No price limits, no T+1. HKEX has neither, so price_limit_pct=None and t_plus_1=False ; the limit and settlement gates simply do not engage. Shorting allowed. Unlike A , long_short=True is accepted. Stamp duty on both sides. HKEX levies 0.10% on buys as well as sells, so TransactionCostModel charges it symmetrically when market == "HK" — the A-share 印花税 stays sell-side only. Per side the preset totals 0.1484%: brokerage 0.04% + stamp duty 0.10% + HKEX trading fee 0.00565% + SFC levy 0.0027% + FRC levy 0.00015%. Total-return basis , same as A , and now genuinely backed by ingested adj_events . store = DataStore(AssayConfig(market="HK", data_dir=Path(os.environ["ASSAY_DATA_DIR_HK"]))) cfg = PortfolioBacktestConfig.preset( "HK", universe="HK100", # or "HSHARE100" for H-shares only period_start="2022-01-01", period_end="2023-12-31", ) Two caveats specific to HK: sector-neutralisation is unavailable (no group labels), and NAV is denominated in HKD with no FX book, so an HK run is not directly comparable to a US or CN one.

title: Tushare data source (China A-share + Hong Kong)
headings: Why CN is sharded per symbol and HK per date
text: Tushare data source (China A-share + Hong Kong) Raw market-data mirror for Chinese A-share and Hong Kong equities, downloaded from the Tushare Pro HTTP API. This is the China/HK analogue of the massive (Polygon, US equities) source: it lands raw provider data on disk, which the Assay ingesters can later normalize into the canonical price_raw / adj_events / universe_snapshots parquet stores ( market=CN / market=HK ). Scope Market Universe Membership history A-share union of CSI300 ( 000300.SH ), CSI500 ( 000905.SH ), CSI1000 ( 000852.SH ) constituents ✅ point-in-time, monthly ( index_weight ) Hong Kong whole market (every name that traded), ranked into HK100 ✅ point-in-time, monthly (turnover-ranked) Hong Kong H-shares (mainland-incorporated issuers), ranked into HSHARE100 ✅ point-in-time, monthly (ISIN CNE + turnover) Hong Kong HSI + Hang Seng TECH constituents ⚠️ current snapshot only (see limitations) Default date range: 2010-01-01 → today . CSI300 membership is stitched from two provider codes: 000300.SH carries weights only from 2016-01, so the SZSE mirror 399300.SZ supplies the 2010-2015 history. They are merged (canonical code wins on overlap) into a single cn/index_weight/CSI300.parquet . CSI500/CSI1000 need only one code each (CSI1000's series starts at its 2014-10 inception). Endpoint and credentials By default the token is spent against https://api.tushare.pro . Set TUSHARE_API_URL (or Data Settings → Tushare → API Endpoint in the WebUI) to route the same calls through a relay/cache gateway that speaks the identical {api_name, params, fields} protocol. Gateways authenticate on an X-API-Key header rather than the body token ; the client sends the credential both ways, so one configuration works against either endpoint. This matters because the HK price endpoints are not permissioned on a plain Tushare token — hk_daily , hk_adjfactor and hk_daily_adj all need an entitled endpoint. Without one, only the HK index value series is reachable. Running # from the repo root, with the project venv TUSHARE_TOKEN=xxxx TUSHARE_API_URL=https://your-gateway/v1/tushare/query PYTHONPATH=src \ /data/haoluo/_assay_venv/bin/python scripts/download_tushare.py --markets hk The job is resumable : each per-symbol / per-index parquet is skipped if it already exists, so re-running the same command continues an interrupted backfill. Pass --force to overwrite. Useful flags: Incremental daily refresh. Because resume skips existing per-symbol files, this standalone script only backfills — it will not extend a symbol's file with new dates. For an incremental update, use the WebUI Data → Update job (or orchestrate.run(..., mode="update") ): it fetches the new window by trade-date (all symbols per API call) via run_cn_by_date and appends to the raw files — a few calls instead of one per symbol. See Data Pipeline → Data Manager . --markets cn,hk — pick markets (or use --steps for fine control) --steps cn_universe,cn_prices,... — explicit step list (see ALL_STEPS ) --start 20100101 --end 20260627 — date window --rate 380 --workers 8 — API calls/min budget and concurrency --api-url URL — endpoint override (default $TUSHARE_API_URL ) --limit-symbols N — cap the universe for a quick smoke test Set --rate to the endpoint's real per-minute ceiling. A gateway that answers HTTP 429 is telling you the budget is too high; the client waits out the Retry-After rather than backing off exponentially, but a chronically over-budget rate still costs throughput. On-disk layout ( $TUSHARE_DATA_DIR , default /data/tushare_data ) _manifest.json run config, row counts, failures, history meta/ stock_basic.parquet A-share listings (L + D + P) — names, list/delist dates hk_basic.parquet HK listings (L + D — delisted included, no survivorship bias) trade_cal.parquet SSE trading calendar hk_trade_cal.parquet HKEX trading calendar cn/ index_weight/CSI300.parquet monthly constituent + weight history ... index_weight/CSI500.parquet index_weight/CSI1000.parquet universe.parquet deduped union (ts_code, indices, first_date, last_date) daily/{ts_code}.parquet raw OHLCV (unadjusted): open/high/low/close/pre_close/vol/amount adj_factor/{ts_code}.parquet split/merge adjustment factor (for qfq/hfq) daily_basic/{ts_code}.parquet PE/PB/PS/turnover/total_mv/circ_mv/total_share/float_share/... dividend/{ts_code}.parquet cash + stock dividends and split ratios hk/ index_global/HSI.parquet index value series index_global/HSTECH.parquet constituents.parquet current-snapshot HSI/HSTECH membership (ts_code, index, name) daily/{YYYY}/{YYYYMMDD}.parquet raw HK OHLCV (unadjusted), whole market per date adj_factor/{YYYY}/{YYYYMMDD}.parquet cum_adjfactor + close_price, whole market per date daily_adj/{YYYY}/{YYYYMMDD}.parquet total_mv/free_mv/total_share/turnover_ratio per date logs/ failures_*.txt per-step symbol failures (if any) Files are zstd-compressed parquet (project convention). Columns are the raw Tushare fields , unmodified, for fidelity — adjustment/normalization happens downstream in the Assay ingest layer, not here. Why CN is sharded per symbol and HK per date CN membership is known up front ( index_weight ), so the downloader can iterate a symbol list. HK has no membership API at all , so there is no list to iterate: the tradable universe has to be discovered from whole-market by-date responses. Storing those responses as-is costs one API call per trading day per endpoint (~4,100 days x 3 = ~12,300 calls for 2010→today) and yields a mirror that is survivorship-free by construction — a name that delisted in 2014 is still in every file up to its last trading day. It also makes resume and incremental update the same code path: a date whose file exists is skipped, so re-running only fetches the new tail. Adjustment (splits / dividends / merges) A-share prices in cn/daily are unadjusted . To build forward/back-adjusted series, combine them with cn/adj_factor (Tushare's cumulative factor) or derive events from cn/dividend ( stk_div , stk_bo_rate , stk_co_rate for splits/bonus, cash_div for cash). This matches Assay's adj_events model, which recomputes the cumulative factor from primitive events rather than trusting a provider's cumulative number. HK corporate actions Tushare gives HK no dividend or split records — only a cumulative hk_adjfactor . The ingest layer therefore reconstructs events from its steps: where the factor moves from f_prev to f , the total price ratio is r = f / f_prev , and prices strictly before that date scale by 1 / r . Two vendor artifacts make a naive reading of the factor wrong, so each step is cross-checked against hk_daily.pre_close (which is restated onto the post-action basis on an action day) and dropped unless the two agree within 1%: the factor is occasionally re-anchored on a date with no corporate action, which would otherwise fabricate a double-digit dividend; pre_close itself drifts a tick off the prior close on sub-HK$1 names, so it is used only as a corroborating witness, never for the magnitude. Surviving steps are attributed to a share change ( split_ratio = r ) when the factor fell, when hk/daily_adj 's share count moved materially, or when that share count is unavailable ; only a step whose share count is known and flat becomes a cash distribution of close_prev * (1 - 1/r) . Defaulting to a share event is the safe way to be wrong. The total-return series is exact under either attribution, but adj="split" is the default read basis ( AssayConfig.default_adj ), and misreading a 2-for-1 split as a dividend would book half the share price as cash and leave the raw split gap in the split-only panel — every factor would then read a fabricated -50% return. The opposite error merely over-adjusts the split-only view by a dividend. The ingester logs a warning counting any steps it could not attribute from share data. Two hard preconditions follow from adj_events being an upsert-only store — a bad event cannot be withdrawn by a later run, only by deleting the store: hk/daily must be present or no events are written at all (without pre_close there is nothing to corroborate against, and a vendor re-anchor would become a permanent double-digit phantom dividend); an incomplete hk/daily_adj degrades the split/total distinction but never fabricates a payout. Note that hk_daily_adj 's own close / adj_factor columns are not a usable adjusted series: they do not compose across share consolidations. Use hk_adjfactor , whose close_price reconciles exactly with hk_daily.close . A consolidation is normally executed while the stock is halted , so the steps with the largest ratios are exactly the ones with no hk_daily bar to witness them. Those are corroborated against the factor feed's own restated close_price instead, and accepted only when the ratio is extreme enough (≥2x either way) to be unambiguously a share change — a near-1 ratio on a non-trading day cannot be told apart from a re-anchor, and skipping a small dividend is a 2% error where missing a consolidation is a 40x one. Measured accuracy Against the exchange's own daily returns ( close / pre_close ), over the 487 names that have ever been in HK100, 2010-2026, 1.45M bars: deviation bars share > 0.1% 1,892 0.13% > 1% 1,117 0.077% > 20% 23 0.0016% Restricted to a recent month's 300 most-traded names, 0 mismatches (max 6e-05). The 23 worst are split roughly evenly between two causes, both inherent to the vendor feed rather than to the reconstruction: pre_close is simply wrong on some thin days (e.g. 01063.HK reported a HK$0.01 prior close for a stock trading at HK$0.22). Here the reconstructed series is the correct one and the reference is the bad number. cum_adjfactor misses an action that pre_close did record — spin-offs in particular (e.g. 00004.HK 's November 2017 demerger). Because events are sourced from factor steps, an action absent from the factor feed is absent from adj_events too, leaving the raw gap. Sourcing events from pre_close restatements as well would close this, and is the obvious next improvement. Neither residual is material to a ranked factor (the default signal_transform is rank ), but both matter to anything that consumes raw returns. Known limitations HK index membership is a current snapshot, not history. Tushare exposes no index-membership interface for HSI or Hang Seng TECH ( index_member / index_basic market=HK return nothing). Those two universes are therefore a single current constituent list vendored in src/assay/data/tushare/constituents.py (captured 2026-06-27), and backtests over them are survivorship-biased . Prefer HK100 , which the ingest layer derives point-in-time from realised turnover (see Multi-market ). No HK industry classification. hk_basic carries no industry field and Tushare has no HK equivalent of the A-share classification, so no security_groups store is written for market=HK . Sector neutralization is honestly unavailable there rather than silently a no-op. Hang Seng TECH index code. On index_global the Hang Seng TECH value series is HKTECH (not HSTECH , which returns nothing). The friendly name HSTECH is used for the on-disk file and constituent list. HK prices are HKD only. No FX book exists, so a HK backtest's NAV is in HKD and is not comparable to a US or CN run without converting outside Assay.

title: Agent-native factor research
text: Agent-native factor research Assay provides durable research state and an execution environment for external agents. The caller chooses its model, prompts and search strategy. Existing evaluation APIs and temporary assay.Session panel caches remain available. Python workflow For an offline smoke demo with synthetic prices and two simulated agent clients: PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/demo_agent_research.py . It uses the real evaluator, retains a failed attempt, reconstructs the service, and continues a saved session. This exercises lifecycle behavior; it does not validate real LLM compatibility. Install pip install -e '.[mcp,perf]' and prepare market data using Getting Started . Dataset registration does not download data. import assay assay.init() # ASSAY_DATA_DIR and market configuration ws = assay.research_workspace() dataset = ws.register_dataset( "nasdaq-reversal-2024", "NASDAQ100", ["2024-01-01", "2024-12-31"], horizons=[1, 5, 10], execution="next_open", adj="split", ) session = ws.create_session(dataset["id"], "Study short-term reversal", agent="agent-a", max_experiments=20) first = ws.evaluate( session["id"], "-cs_rank(ts_returns(close,5))", "Recent winners may reverse", request_id="reversal-5d-01", agent="agent-a", ) ws.add_note(session["id"], "Compare shorter lookbacks next", agent="agent-a") second = ws.evaluate( session["id"], "-cs_rank(ts_returns(close,3))", "Shorter windows may reduce delay", request_id="reversal-3d-01", parent_id=first["id"], agent="agent-b", ) print(ws.compare_experiments([first["id"], second["id"]])) In local or service-key mode, state lives at <data_dir>/research/workspace.sqlite3 . After restarting, use ws.list_sessions() and ws.get_session(id) to recover the goal, dataset, notes, all attempts and remaining budget. Every new request has its own experiment ID, even when the expression is identical to an earlier attempt. Factor selection and portfolio evidence New built-in assay datasets with next-day execution run both factor diagnostics and a portfolio backtest. report.portfolio contains cost-adjusted NAV, return, Sharpe, drawdown, trading turnover and cost drag. Portfolio settings are frozen in the dataset hash. For example, pass portfolio={"rebalance_type": "weekly"} when registering a dataset. portfolio={"enabled": False} selects diagnostics only; explicit IC scoring windows and same-day close diagnostics use this mode by default. Existing saved dataset specifications retain their original settings. Reports record absent impact/capital inputs and held positions with missing quotes. Every parseable attempt registers its canonical factor in the workspace's FactorDB registry in the same SQLite transaction. A factor can have many attempts and many sessions; the complete reports remain in the experiment history. The registry's latest score is a discovery view, not the experimental history. decision = ws.decide_candidate( second["id"], "accepted", "Keep the shorter lookback for further research", request_id="select-reversal-3d", agent="agent-b", ) print(ws.list_candidates(session["id"])) print(ws.factor_history(second["factor_id"])) Decisions are append-only and scoped to a factor within one session. Supported states are candidate , accepted , rejected and archived . Each decision points to an experiment and records its reason, author and retry identity. Acceptance requires a completed experiment. Decisions do not consume experiment budget and survive restart, export and import. Handoff context omits rejected and archived factors from its active candidate ranking. assay_candidate_decide , assay_candidate_list and assay_factor_history expose these operations over MCP. The workbench displays portfolio metrics and records human selection decisions through the same REST workspace. fdb_query and fdb_factor discover both the research registry and the optional compute registry with source="all" (default), "research" or "compute" . Compute submission and node-value storage still require the configured FactorDB/ADES backend; discovery does not copy nodes or merge the two physical databases. next_open executes after the signal date and attributes overnight returns to the old book and intraday returns to the executed book. next_close enters at the next day's close, including in IC labels. Corrected daily evaluation settings carry evaluation_protocol="assay-daily-v2" ; old next_close datasets must be registered again. Their stored reports remain readable. Compute score keys also version this execution convention, so old labels cannot satisfy new requests from cache. Observed panel hashes include prices, membership and group labels. Precomputed subtrees retain pre-admission rolling history, and membership is applied when computing cross-sectional operators and final outputs. Matching replay hashes verify the observed input content; they do not create a physical market-data archive. Run scripts/validate_research_loop.py --data-root PREPARED_STORE --output NEW_DIR to check the loop against real prepared data. Outputs include session manifests, source and implementation hashes, cash/share accounting reconciliation, and separate timings for complete research attempts, fresh factor matrices, shared panel/CSE matrix batches and exact result-cache hits. Matrix throughput is not end-to-end backtest throughput. The independent ledger checks NAV using recorded fills; portfolio selection and vendor data completeness need separate validation. Scoring windows and expression contracts period is the data-read interval, including warmup and forward-label buffers. Register score_period and sorted score_dates to compute headline IC/RankIC only on independently frozen trading dates. Explicit scoring currently supports one horizon. Missing dates, null scores, misaligned arrays or extra in-window dates produce a retained INCOMPLETE_SCORE_COVERAGE failure, never an aggregate fallback. The experiment's report contains scoped metrics and dates; panel_report retains the original backend evidence. Turnover, quintile returns and decay are set to null in the scoped report because daily IC arrays cannot recompute those metrics. dataset = ws.register_dataset( "reversal-scoped", "NASDAQ100", ["2024-01-01", "2024-08-02"], horizons=[1], score_period=["2024-07-01", "2024-07-02"], score_dates=["2024-07-01", "2024-07-02"], expression_policy={ "fields": ["close", "volume"], "operators": ["ts_returns", "ts_mean", "cs_rank", "neg"], "max_window": 60, "max_cumulative_lookback": 100, }, ) Obtain the expected trading dates from a verified calendar before registration. Both the scoring scope and expression policy participate in spec_hash . The workspace enforces field/operator whitelists and nested window budgets before calling the backend. Rejected candidates remain failed attempts and consume one attempt unit, but do not execute a market evaluation. These window-budget rules match the stable AlphaBench OHLCV grammar; they are not an exact finite-history claim for recursive filters such as EMA. The same contract applies through SDK and MCP. Dataset registration specifies warmup/buffer bounds; it does not infer or download extra history automatically. Search checkpoints and multi-window programs Clients can save their own MCTS tree, EA population, generation and random state as a JSON object. Assay stores an append-only checkpoint stream per session and name. This is storage for a client-defined algorithm, not automatic serialization or execution of arbitrary Python objects. Save only JSON data, never credentials. context = ws.research_context(session_id) saved = ws.save_checkpoint(session_id, 'search', 'mcts', {'nodes': [{'experiment_id': experiment_id, 'visits': 3}], 'rng': [1, 2]}, request_id='checkpoint-1', expected_revision=0, expected_state_revision=context['state_revision']) restored = ws.get_checkpoint(session_id, 'search') expected_revision fences conflicting writers. The optional state revision fences changes between reading the session and saving. Retry a timed-out save with the same request ID and inputs. get_checkpoint reports changes to the session plus new attempts and status changes; clients must reconcile those records before continuing. A checkpoint can be saved during an in-flight attempt, but it does not resolve that attempt. Individual JSON states are limited to 1 MiB. Session manifests include checkpoints when present; older manifests remain importable. Checkpoint content is client-supplied and its watermark cannot prove that the algorithm state incorporated every attempt. A research program links separate sessions while preserving their individual dataset specifications and budgets. Evaluate a completed factor again with reassess_program_factor , then inspect program_factor_history : program = ws.create_program('momentum', 'Study signal persistence', request_id='program-1') ws.attach_program_session(program['id'], train_session_id, label='train') ws.attach_program_session(program['id'], later_session_id, label='later') result = ws.reassess_program_factor(program['id'], source_experiment_id, later_session_id, request_id='later-1') history = ws.program_factor_history(program['id'], result['attempt']['factor_id']) pool = ws.program_candidates(program['id']) comparison = ws.compare_program_windows(program['id'], source_experiment_id, result['attempt']['id'], drop_threshold=0.02) Reassessment uses the target session's settings and budget. The history preserves window, settings, metrics and source links. The comparison uses a caller-selected RankIC drop threshold and requires ordered, non-overlapping scoring windows and matching settings. Non-overlapping scoring dates do not verify forward-label availability or a trading-session embargo. Its flag is descriptive, not a statistical decay test. Program membership and cross-session links are stored in the workspace database; session manifests transfer individual sessions and checkpoints; program manifests also transfer membership and reassessment links. Market snapshots remain a separate responsibility. The corresponding MCP tools are assay_checkpoint_save , assay_checkpoint_get , assay_checkpoint_list , assay_program_create , assay_program_list , assay_program_get , assay_program_export , assay_program_import , assay_program_attach_session , assay_program_reassess and assay_program_factor_history , assay_program_candidates and assay_program_compare_windows . Factor decisions remain scoped to each session. REST routes are listed in the REST guide . MCP workflow Start assay serve-mcp . The research operations include: Tool Purpose assay_backend_list Discover adapters and optionally check availability assay_research_context Read compact, evidence-linked handoff context assay_research_import Restore a manifest into another workspace without resetting budget assay_research_export Export full session state with a SHA-256 integrity hash assay_experiment_replay Explicitly rerun a terminal attempt under the same spec assay_dataset_register Register fixed daily evaluation settings assay_dataset_list Discover registered datasets assay_research_session_create Start a goal with an attempt budget assay_research_session_list Discover saved research sessions assay_research_session_get Recover context, notes and attempts assay_research_note Record decisions and handoff instructions assay_experiment_run Evaluate and persist a hypothesis and expression assay_experiment_get Read compact metrics, costs and failures; page through detailed evidence assay_experiment_compare Compare metrics and specification compatibility assay_experiment_abandon Explicitly close an interrupted synchronous attempt assay_candidate_decide Append an evidence-linked acceptance, rejection, archive or reopening assay_candidate_list List canonical candidates and their current session decisions assay_factor_history Page a factor's attempt summaries and decision history assay_experiment_reconcile Recover/poll a durable asynchronous attempt assay_experiment_cancel Persist a reason and cancel asynchronous task acceptance An agent discovers live universes, registers a dataset, starts or resumes a session, reads prior attempts, lints candidates, executes an experiment, inspects evidence, and records its next decision. It can then revise, call the existing portfolio tools, or stop. There is no provider call or fixed search algorithm in the workspace. assay_experiment_get(id) now returns a compact summary by default. Request section="trades" , "positions" , "nav" , "ic" or "diagnostics" with offset and limit (1–100) to inspect details. Pages include total and next_offset . This keeps large backtests within model context limits. The Python workspace and REST experiment endpoint retain full reports. For long sessions, use assay_research_context for model input; session export and the complete session tool return bulk evidence for storage and analysis. assay_factor_history also accepts offset and limit , paging both chronological lists. Its history_page reports separate experiment and decision totals. Retry, failure and recovery An attempt transitions from running to completed or failed ; explicit recovery may change synchronous running to abandoned , or asynchronous running to cancelled . Completed means the evaluator returned without a failure mode, not that the factor is profitable or statistically validated. Use a stable request_id per attempt. Retrying it returns saved state without executing again, including when still running. Different inputs under the same request ID are rejected. SQLite reservations enforce budgets across processes; Failed, abandoned and cancelled attempts consume budget. Terminal experiments are not overwritten by subsequent runs, and notes are appended through the API. A synchronous worker interruption leaves a running record. Confirm the worker has stopped, abandon the attempt with a reason, then retry with a new request ID. Abandoning a record does not cancel a live backend. Backend exceptions and diagnostic failures are retained for the next agent to inspect. Alternative backends and evidence boundaries Implement ResearchBackend.evaluate(expr, dataset) -> dict , returning a JSON-safe factor report ( failure_mode , metrics and optional diagnostics). Then call ws.register_backend("team", my_backend) and register datasets with backend="team" . Backend names are persisted; objects and credentials must be re-registered per serving process. QFV can be integrated at this boundary; this change does not install a QFV execution adapter. Custom datasets can include JSON-safe backend_options , which participate in the specification hash. The built-in evaluator rejects unsupported options. assay.integrations.alphabench.AlphaBenchBackend is an optional adapter to AlphaBench V2's patched localhost:8002 Assay service; it verifies the registered endpoint, frozen universe date, symbol-axis hash/count and data cutoff before exposing successful reports. It requires AlphaBench's Python package at runtime. Datasets are immutable specifications , not immutable copies of market data. Their SHA-256 spec_hash covers backend name, universe, dates, cutoff, horizons, execution, adjustment and optional snapshot reference. It excludes market-data contents, backend code and model behavior. Matching specs do not certify unchanged underlying data or out-of-sample validity. Comparisons retain failed rows and flag mismatched specs, without ranking incompatible experiments. The built-in Assay backend cannot resolve snapshot IDs and rejects them. Custom backends must resolve and verify any supplied snapshot_id . Existing end-date universe selection is unchanged. Train/test isolation, selection-bias control and portfolio validation remain explicit research choices. Budgets cover evaluator attempts, not tokens, wall time or portfolio tool calls. Automatic general-purpose agent runners, built-in token billing and dedicated research-session WebUI/REST surfaces are not implemented in this version. Discovery, handoff and explicit reruns Call assay_backend_list(probe=True) before choosing a backend. The response separates declared capabilities from checked availability and shows backend names referenced by persisted datasets even when their adapters have not been registered after restart. Local checks inspect prepared files; remote checks inspect service inventory. Neither certifies coverage of a requested period. Adapters may optionally implement describe() -> dict and probe() -> dict ; plain evaluate() adapters remain supported. Use assay_research_context(session_id, limit=10) for handoff: it returns remaining budget, failure counts, normalized expression repeats, notes and candidate summaries without metric time series. Each list is limited to 1–50 rows, with truncation flags. Individual text fields are not token-limited. Ranking uses absolute RankIC and is descriptive; syntactic duplicates do not measure factor correlation. backends = ws.list_backends(probe=True) context = ws.research_context(session_id, limit=10) manifest = ws.export_session(session_id) assert ws.verify_manifest(manifest) rerun = ws.replay_experiment(experiment_id, session_id, request_id="explicit-rerun-1", agent="next-agent") The export reads one consistent SQLite snapshot and has a stable hash until records change. It includes complete research records, not market-data bytes or adapter code. The hash checks integrity, not source authenticity; use assay_research_import to restore records into another workspace. A replay preserves the source expression, hypothesis and spec hash, records replay_of , and spends a new budget unit. It can target another session with an identical dataset specification. Reusing its request ID returns the saved attempt. Mutable data may change the result. This does not restore an agent's search tree. Migrating a session Call target.import_session(manifest) or MCP assay_research_import(manifest) to restore a version-1 manifest. The importer validates integrity, structure, dataset specification hash, attempt identities, lineage and budget before writing one atomic transaction. It retains original IDs, request IDs, notes, timestamps and all terminal attempts. Importing the exact same state again is idempotent. Existing conflicting records, including a session that has advanced since export, are rejected without overwriting or merging. Backends need not be registered to read imported records; register the matching backend and make its data available before evaluating again. Running attempts cannot be migrated. Reconcile or cancel asynchronous attempts; for synchronous attempts, confirm the worker stopped and explicitly abandon them. Export after the records reach terminal states. External replay_of references are retained as provenance; the source session is not automatically imported. When the source is available, its status, expression, hypothesis and specification must match, in either import order. A missing external source must be imported separately if it needs to be inspected. Hashes do not authenticate historical reports. Importing records does not transfer a running agent, its search tree or data. Import does not disable the source workspace. Budgets apply within each workspace; choose where to continue after migration. This is snapshot copying, not distributed worker coordination or a global budget service. Durable asynchronous research Configure the FactorDB controller with ASSAY_FACTORDB_DIR , ASSAY_QFV_PANEL_DIR , ASSAY_ADES=1 , and separate worker credentials ( ASSAY_WORKER_KEYS ). Run an ADES worker against the same panel version. Probe assay_backend_list(probe=true) and copy its factordb_ades data version into snapshot_id when registering the dataset. The SDK equivalent is: ws = service.research version = ws.backends["factordb_ades"].probe()["data_version"] dataset = ws.register_dataset( "panel-reversal", "TOP500", ["2024-12-02", "2025-01-24"], backend="factordb_ades", snapshot_id=version, adj="total", horizons=[1], ) session = ws.create_session(dataset["id"], "Test short-term reversal", max_experiments=6) attempt = ws.evaluate(session["id"], "-ts_delta(close, 2)", "Recent moves may reverse", request_id="candidate-1") # Later, including after constructing a new service/workspace process: attempt = ws.reconcile_experiment(attempt["id"]) Use dates/universe supported by your own panel. This backend requires total adjustment and as_of=end , and rejects score windows and custom backend options. It pins the logical panel version, without hashing or freezing physical files. Results contain aggregate FactorDB diagnostics, not the full synchronous report. A changed controller version rejects a new submission; an already submitted attempt keeps its original result version. The MCP operation is assay_experiment_reconcile(experiment_id) ; REST exposes POST /v1/research/experiments/{id}/reconcile . The workbench offers Reconcile asynchronous jobs . Reconciliation is explicit: reads do not poll the backend. A transient error retains a running attempt and includes code , retryable , and recommended_action . Correct deterministic input failures in a new attempt, linking the failed attempt as its parent. Active asynchronous jobs cannot be abandoned; use tracked cancellation instead. Keep registry, queue and research databases when restarting; exporting a completed manifest preserves records, not worker processes or physical market data. Portfolio accounting protocol Portfolio targets are fractions of pre-trade NAV. Executed quantities are preserved when transaction costs are charged to cash; resulting weights are recalculated against post-fee NAV. Long-only, unlevered books reserve cash for costs. Explicitly leveraged or long-short books can borrow. New datasets and portfolio attempts record portfolio_accounting_protocol: cash-funded-v1 , also discoverable in the Assay backend capabilities. Existing sessions can continue using their original dataset: historical records remain unchanged and new attempts record the current protocol. Comparisons flag different accounting protocols as not directly comparable; replay requires the original protocol. Set portfolio.initial_capital to a positive amount in the market currency to apply minimum commissions and enable trailing liquidity for newly registered datasets. At each rebalance, participation is the order value divided by the average unadjusted daily close × volume over the preceding adv_window exchange sessions (20 by default); the execution day is excluded. It uses the current portfolio NAV, caps fills at max_adv_fraction , and applies the configured slippage model to filled participation. Missing or incomplete history blocks affected orders. partial_fill_handling="force" bypasses the capacity cap and produces a warning. Reported liquidity evidence includes coverage, blocked orders and whether impact was applied. Market-data vendors can revise historical bars; this calculation alone does not guarantee point-in-time revision history. US and HK volumes default to shares. For A-shares, set liquidity_volume_multiplier explicitly: use 100 for a Tushare volume in lots, or 1 if volume is already in shares. For example: portfolio={"initial_capital": 1000000, "liquidity_volume_multiplier": 100} . An explicit liquidity_model: null disables automatic liquidity. Without capital or participation input, capacity and market impact are not applied; the report warns. Existing frozen dataset settings are preserved. The REST portfolio endpoint enables the model for inline requests with capital; a nested config is replayed verbatim and must explicitly include liquidity_model and the volume multiplier. Account workspaces and shared resources With account authentication enabled, REST and HTTP MCP use the authenticated account identity to select a private persistent research workspace; a user's login and personal API keys access the same workspace. A service key accesses the original shared service workspace, so keep it as a privileged integration credential. The first upgrade adds a persistent random identity to each account; existing browser sessions must sign in again. Account database and workspace data should be backed up and restored together. Earlier experimental account directories keyed by numeric user ID are not automatically assigned to the new identities; an administrator must verify ownership and migrate any needed records explicitly. Old shared sessions remain there; an administrator can export an individual session and import it into the correct account after checking ownership. Local Python and unauthenticated deployments retain a shared local workspace.
