Research datasets, sessions, experiments, notes, the research factor registry, the factor library, saved combinations, temporary panel sessions and calculation caches are account-scoped. Personal workspaces can reuse their own research panels and cached values. Market data and physical compute remain shared. The original library and combinations remain accessible to the service key; account workspaces begin with their own empty stores. With FactorDB and ADES configured, a personal account can use its own FactorDB registry and the factordb_ades research backend. Jobs, scores, factor metadata, novelty fingerprints and compute usage remain account-scoped; the ADES queue and workers are shared. Workers and server operators can see the expressions they execute and must be trusted. ASSAY_FACTORDB_BUDGET_S can set a per-owner daily compute budget, checked before submission; hard CPU, memory and storage quotas are not provided. Temporary panel sessions live in one process: route requests for a session to the same worker, and recreate it after a restart. Durable research sessions, saved factors and combinations persist across workers and restarts. To enable private distributed research, configure ASSAY_FACTORDB_DIR , ASSAY_QFV_PANEL_DIR and ASSAY_ADES=1 on the controller, and connect workers using ASSAY_WORKER_KEYS . A personal account can call /v1/fdb/markets or assay_backend_list(probe=true) to obtain the data version, then register a research dataset with backend="factordb_ades" , snapshot_id set to that version, adj="total" and as_of equal to the end date. Submit and reconcile attempts through the usual research REST or MCP tools. Personal /v1/fdb/* and fdb_* calls use the same private compute registry. Without ADES, these compute operations report that the private backend is unavailable; the local Assay research backend remains usable. Private ADES jobs require updated workers that support lease tokens. For ordinary ADES-backed fdb_submit , provide a client-generated request_id and reuse it with identical inputs when retrying. REST POST /v1/fdb/submit and MCP fdb_submit share the same account-scoped request record. A repeated key with different inputs returns a conflict. Without a key, a retry can create another job; in non-ADES mode the new request_id option is not supported. Cancel asynchronous research result = ws.cancel_experiment(attempt["id"], "Research direction changed") # After an outage/restart, reconciliation resumes the saved cancellation intent. result = ws.reconcile_experiment(attempt["id"]) MCP exposes assay_experiment_cancel(experiment_id, reason) . REST exposes POST /v1/research/experiments/{id}/cancel with {"reason": "..."} . In the workbench, select a running experiment, expand Cancel an asynchronous experiment , enter its reason and click Cancel selected asynchronous experiment . The first reason is retained across retries. The adapter publishes supports_cancellation=true . Cancellation stops queued work and revokes leases, including a dispatch delayed until after cancellation. Remote native computation already running may finish; its results are rejected. A completion accepted first remains completed. Temporary failures keep the cancellation intent in a running record; reconcile it instead of submitting a replacement under the same request. A cancelled attempt is terminal and exportable, retains its attempt-budget charge, and can be the parent of a new revision. Cancellation creates no factor score and does not cache a failed evaluation. Daily compute usage counts accepted result receipts; discarded in-flight computation is not metered. Synchronous backends return CANCELLATION_UNSUPPORTED ; inspect the worker before explicitly abandoning an interrupted synchronous record. Moving a research program Use assay_program_export to capture the program, linked sessions, checkpoints, decisions and reassessment links in one manifest. Use assay_program_import to restore it atomically into another workspace. Identical imports can be retried; conflicting identities and running attempts are rejected. The manifest records dataset specifications, not market files or backend software. Arrange those separately before running new experiments. The digest checks integrity, not origin.

title: Research audit for judges
text: Research audit for judges An audit turns a research session into a compact, evidence-linked review packet. It checks the saved records without calling a model, executing a backend, changing candidate decisions or consuming experiment budget. The same implementation serves MCP, REST, the Python workspace, the workbench and offline manifests. Run an audit In the workbench, select a session and click Audit session . The panel shows check results, errors, review items and candidate evidence. Download audit JSON preserves the server response and its content hash. Download the session manifest alongside it to give a judge the underlying evidence. MCP clients call the read-only, idempotent assay_research_audit tool: {"session_id":"research_...","offset":0,"limit":20} The deployed HTTP API exposes the same packet: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ASSAY_MCP_API_KEY" \ 'https://assay.qfinverse.com/v1/research/sessions/research_.../audit?limit=20' Python callers use their existing workspace: report = service.research.audit_session(session_id) print(report["record_integrity"], report["finding_counts"]) A judge can also audit an exported manifest without a server or market data: python -m assay.audit --manifest session.json --output session.audit.json # Equivalent console entry point after installing the updated package: assay-audit --manifest session.json --output session.audit.json The CLI returns 1 for failed record checks, 0 for consistent records (including review warnings), and 2 for invalid command/input. It refuses to overwrite an existing output file. Offline audits do not import the manifest or open a workspace. What is checked Check Evidence Manifest and specification Envelope/version/hash, dataset hash and record structure Attempts and budget Unique IDs/request IDs, all terminal and running attempts, spent/remaining budget Provenance Session/spec links, canonical expression, parent/replay relationships and time order Lifecycle Candidate decisions point to matching evidence; acceptance needs a completed attempt Diagnostics Saved lookahead flags, scoring completeness and registered expression policy IC metrics Finite values, correlation bounds, aligned dates, score-window bounds and series means Portfolio Saved NAV arithmetic, config/spec consistency, numeric metrics and cost assumptions Local registry Factor-attempt links and experiment/decision identity columns, in the same SQLite snapshot The live database connection is query-only. Cross-session replay sources are checked when present in that snapshot. An offline audit reports an external source as a review item, since that source is absent from the exported session. Registry jobs, score discovery views and usage accounting are outside these registry checks. Failed and cancelled experiments remain in the counts. A recorded experimental failure is not itself an audit failure. Running attempts produce a review item; auditing them neither cancels them nor makes them importable as terminal records. Read the result Field Meaning record_integrity passed or failed saved-record consistency status failed , needs_review or passed ; warnings do not change the integrity verdict checks / finding_counts Whole-session results, independent of pagination findings Stable codes, severity, experiment ID and JSON Pointer evidence locations summary Goal, dataset, budget, all status counts, decisions and candidate metrics assessment Explicit scope and which judgments have not been performed manifest_hash / audit_hash Selected input revision and report content digest Unfrozen data specifications and portfolio execution/cost warnings are review items. They do not imply malformed records. Candidate metrics are descriptive; the audit does not impose a positive-IC threshold or make acceptance decisions for the judge. Backend option values are omitted from the compact summary; the original manifest remains the reference for the complete dataset configuration. Every record is checked even when only one page is returned. page.finding_total and page.candidate_total report separate totals. offset / limit page both lists; has_more and candidates_have_more identify which list continues. Fetch details with the existing experiment and history tools. Pass the first response's manifest_hash as expected_manifest_hash on subsequent calls, or supply --expected-manifest-hash offline. A different snapshot produces EXPECTED_MANIFEST_MISMATCH , preventing a judge from silently combining revisions. The hashes detect content changes; they do not authenticate an author. Replay, market-data authenticity/coverage, out-of-sample validity and goal achievement need their own evidence. The report leaves those judgments explicit in assessment . Related: agent research , MCP , deployment .

title: Reference agent and offline demo
headings: Let a model operate the tools
text: Reference agent and offline demo The reference client provides --preset deepseek-flash for the official DeepSeek Chat Completions API. Set DEEPSEEK_API_KEY in the environment; the preset requests non-thinking mode. Explicit --base-url , --model , --api-key-env , and --extra-body options can override these defaults. Assay's server exposes tools and persists research records. The optional reference client in assay.agent lets a Chat Completions-compatible model choose tools through real stdio or authenticated HTTP MCP. It is replaceable: other MCP clients can use the same research state. Connect to the public server Set the model's ASSAY_AGENT_API_KEY and Assay's separate ASSAY_MCP_API_KEY through your secret manager. MODEL_BASE_URL and MODEL_NAME select your model provider: python -m assay.agent \ --base-url "$MODEL_BASE_URL" --model "$MODEL_NAME" \ --task-file task.txt --output ./remote-agent-run \ --mcp-url https://assay.qfinverse.com/mcp/ \ --mcp-api-key-env ASSAY_MCP_API_KEY --mcp-timeout 300 Choose either --mcp-url or --server-command . Plain HTTP is accepted only for loopback testing. The server owns datasets, budgets, attempts and handoff notes; the local client retains the model conversation and receipts. Before model calls, check the endpoint with the read-only deployment checker . Run the offline demo pip install '.[mcp]' python -m assay.demo --output ./demo-workspace The output directory must not already exist. This generates synthetic OHLCV, executes two factors and a diagnostic failure, restores the session after restart, and writes manifest.json and a portable report.html . No model call or vendor credential is needed. Synthetic prices do not establish investment performance. Let a model operate the tools Prepare a new workspace, then write a text task describing the research goal: python -m assay.demo --prepare-only --output ./agent-workspace export ASSAY_DATA_DIR="$PWD/agent-workspace" # Set DEEPSEEK_API_KEY through your normal secret manager or shell environment. python -m assay.agent \ --base-url https://api.deepseek.com --model deepseek-flash \ --api-key-env DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --extra-body '{"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}' \ --task-file task.txt --output ./agent-run \ --max-turns 8 --max-tool-calls 16 --max-tokens 4096 \ --server-command python -m assay.mcp.server For example, task.txt can ask the agent to discover the synthetic dataset, create a session with a three-attempt budget, test reversal hypotheses, inspect failures and save a handoff note. The client sends only the selected MCP tool schemas and tool results to the configured provider. Research text and reports may therefore leave your machine. API keys remain in environment variables and request headers. --server-command must be the last option. Install the MCP extra in the interpreter used for both the client and server. --extra-body supplies provider-specific settings; it cannot override the model, conversation, tool schema or execution caps. Returned model identity must match the requested name unless explicit --allow-returned-model values are provided. Changing an alias is not evidence of model equivalence. Provider availability and protocol support must be verified for the selected deployment; this client does not make all models interchangeable. Inspect the run tools.json : tool schemas discovered from the server. conversation.json : the messages and tool outputs sent through the loop. run.json : requested configuration, actual response identities, raw received responses, tool results, timing, reported usage and terminal status. The client does not retry HTTP failures or follow redirects. Invalid/truncated responses are retained; they do not execute tool calls. Unknown usage is marked incomplete. A model response without tool calls ends with model_finished , which means the model stopped, not that it achieved the user's objective. Check persisted experiments, notes and reports to evaluate completion. The reference client does not resume a partially recorded conversation; use a new client run and an existing research session for a deliberate handoff. Session budgets remain server-enforced. Routine experiment execution returns compact feedback to the model, while receipts retain the full report. The agent can explicitly request assay_experiment_get for metric series. Session discovery uses compact research context rather than full session exports. This reduces repeated report payloads without changing scores. The reference client normalizes structured JSON and a single JSON text block from MCP before constructing model feedback. Mixed content stays intact. The receipt keeps the original transport payload separately from model_result ; MCP failures reach the model with an explicit isError flag. Compaction happens in this optional client, not in the server: other clients can inspect the full tool response.

title: Research workbench
text: Research workbench Open /#/research on an Assay Web API server. The page reads the same durable research workspace as MCP and the SDK. It shows the research objective, stored experiment activity, parent/replay relationships, full evidence and handoff notes. It does not invent an agent trace or send the browser's objective to an LLM. Local synthetic walkthrough From the repository root, in an environment with Assay's API and MCP extras: pip install '.[api,mcp]' python -m assay.demo --prepare-only --output ./workbench-data export ASSAY_DATA_DIR="$PWD/workbench-data" python -m uvicorn assay.api.app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8014 Visit http://127.0.0.1:8014/#/research . The output directory must be new. The dataset is generated synthetic OHLCV, not historical market evidence. Open Start a new session , choose the synthetic dataset, enter a research goal and an attempt budget, and create the session. Open Evaluate a candidate . Enter a hypothesis and the intentionally invalid expression unknown_operator(close) . Its failure is saved and consumes one attempt, matching the MCP experiment contract. Select that failed attempt as the revision parent. Submit -cs_rank(ts_returns(close,5)) with a revised hypothesis. Inspect its actual scores and the parent relationship. Save a handoff note and download the manifest. Reload the page to verify that the persisted research remains available. All browser-created sessions, experiments and notes are attributed to human:webui . This walkthrough is a real evaluator demonstration driven by human actions; it is not autonomous model evidence. A completed evaluation does not establish profitability or validate the accompanying hypothesis. Observe an agent session Run an MCP agent against the same ASSAY_DATA_DIR , following the reference-agent guide. Select its research session in the workbench. Auto-refresh polls saved state every three seconds; Refresh sessions also discovers newly created sessions. Disabling auto-refresh stops polling after any in-flight read. The page does not start, pause, or resume the agent's conversation. Experiment records are distinct from a complete model/tool execution trace. Click an experiment to inspect the stored payload. Parent relationships are clickable; external replay references remain labeled as references. The dataset configuration belongs to the research session. The top bar's legacy factor-page universe/period selectors are hidden on this page. Request and access behavior Research REST routes live under /v1/research and use the existing API-key configuration. When ASSAY_API_KEYS is set, the Web UI uses its existing assay_api_key local-storage header mechanism. There is no new authorization bypass for reading research data or downloading a manifest. Evaluation runs in the API's thread pool; concurrent reads can display a running attempt. Retrying unchanged inputs after a transport failure retains the same request ID while the page is open. A returned running record retains that ID until a later refresh observes a terminal state. Reloading discards client retry state: inspect persisted attempts before submitting again. There is no automatic worker takeover or durable background-job scheduler in this UI. Browser regression With a server using synthetic data, install Playwright and a compatible Chromium in a separate test environment, then run: python scripts/check_research_workbench_browser.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8014 --output artifacts/workbench-browser The test saves a real workflow screenshot and manifest, verifies its integrity, and imports the downloaded file into a fresh workspace. Downloads preserve the server JSON text so numeric representations covered by the hash remain intact. Separate mock-transport fixtures test pending-request idempotency and slow-list selection races; those fixtures are never presented as real model or market experiments.

title: Factor Combination
text: Factor Combination Blend several single factors into one composite alpha and score it honestly out-of-sample. The combination layer follows the standard quant-research protocol — fit on train, select on validation, report on test — so the test IC you read is not contaminated by the fitting. It is exposed three ways over one shared engine: WebUI — the Factor Combination tab. REST — POST /v1/combination (and GET /v1/combination/methods ). SDK — AssayService.combine_factors(...) . Pipeline For each rebalance the constituents go through: Standardize — every factor is z-scored ( zscore ) or ranked ( rank ) cross-sectionally per day, so factors on different scales blend sanely. NaN-aware: a symbol missing on a date stays out of that day's cross-section. Orient — each factor is flipped to point at positive train IC ; the orientation ( +1 / -1 ) is reported so the weights stay readable. Fit on TRAIN only — combination weights (or a model) are learned on the train window. Select on VALIDATION — with method="auto" , every candidate is fit on train and the one with the best validation ICIR is kept. Score on TEST — the frozen composite's IC / RankIC / ICIR is reported on the untouched test window. Embargo — the last embargo days of the train and validation blocks are purged (default = the largest forward horizon) so an overlapping horizon- h label can never leak across a split boundary (the "purged" split). The composite is a (T, N) signal evaluated everywhere with the same weights; only the fit used the train window. Methods Analytic / optimization (always available — numpy + scipy) Method What it does equal equal blend of the oriented factors ic_weight weight ∝ mean train IC magnitude icir_weight weight ∝ train ICIR (mean IC / std IC) — default ; rewards stable predictors ols pooled cross-sectional regression of forward returns on the factors ridge L2-regularized regression ( ridge_lambda ); robust to collinear factors nnls non-negative least squares — a constrained (long-only) optimization max_icir Grinold's Σ⁻¹·IC̄ — the linear blend that maximizes the combination's IC information ratio These produce an explicit per-factor weight ; the composite is the linear blend Σ wₖ·factorₖ . Learned models (qlib-style — optional libraries) The composite is the model's prediction of the forward return from the oriented factors, so the per-factor numbers reported are feature importances , not linear weights. Method Library Kind linear , lasso , elastic_net scikit-learn linear random_forest , extra_trees scikit-learn tree ensemble gbrt , hist_gbrt scikit-learn gradient boosting mlp scikit-learn neural net lightgbm lightgbm gradient boosting xgboost xgboost gradient boosting A model appears in GET /v1/combination/methods (and the WebUI dropdown) only when its library is installed: pip install scikit-learn lightgbm xgboost Hyper-parameters can be overridden per call via model_params (e.g. {"n_estimators": 500, "max_depth": 6, "learning_rate": 0.03} ); sensible defaults are used otherwise, and every model is fit with a fixed seed so a run is a pure function of its inputs. REST curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/combination \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{ "factors": ["rank(close)", "alpha101:1", "lib:<factor_id>", {"name": "mom", "expr": "delta(close, 10)"}], "train": ["2025-01-02", "2025-10-31"], "val": ["2025-11-01", "2026-01-31"], "test": ["2026-02-01", "2026-06-09"], "universe": "NASDAQ100", "horizons": [1, 5, 10], "method": "auto" }' # which methods are installed? curl localhost:8000/v1/combination/methods Saving & reloading runs Every run auto-saves as the rolling "last run"; save a named, reloadable record — with the fitted model (weights/importances, orientation, selection scores, scorecard) — and list or reload them later without recomputing. curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/combination/saved -d '{"name":"my blend","result":<result-json>}' curl localhost:8000/v1/combination/saved # list summaries curl localhost:8000/v1/combination/saved/<id> # full record (the model) curl -X DELETE localhost:8000/v1/combination/saved -d '{"ids":["<id>"]}' SDK equivalents on AssayService : save_combination(result, name) , list_combinations() , get_combination(id) , delete_combinations(ids) — backed by CombinationStore under <data_dir>/combinations/ . Factor specs accept: a bare expression ( "rank(close)" ), a library reference ( "lib:<factor_id>" ), an Alpha catalog number ( "alpha101:<n>" / "alpha158:<n>" ), or a dict {"name": ..., "expr": ...} / {"name": ..., "id": ...} . Response (shape) { "method": "ridge", // the chosen scheme (auto resolves it) "weight_kind": "weight", // "weight" (linear) | "importance" (learned model) "standardize": "zscore", "horizon": 1, "factor_names": ["rank(close)", "alpha101_1", "mom"], "weights": { "rank(close)": 0.41, "alpha101_1": 0.33, "mom": 0.26 }, "orientation": { "rank(close)": 1.0, "alpha101_1": -1.0, "mom": 1.0 }, "per_factor_train_ic": { "...": 0.012 }, "train": { "n_dates": 170, "ic": 0.018, "icir": 0.21, "rank_ic": 0.020, "rank_icir": 0.24 }, "val": { "...": "..." }, "test": { "...": "..." }, // the headline, out-of-sample numbers "selection": { "equal": 0.18, "ridge": 0.21, "...": "..." }, // present when method="auto" "splits": { "train": ["..."], "val": ["..."], "test": ["..."], "embargo": 10 }, "resolved_factors": [{ "name": "...", "expr": "..." }], "dropped": [{ "name": "alpha101_25", "failure_mode": "..." }], // didn't evaluate "diagnostics": { "composite_turnover_1d": 0.08, "...": "..." } } Non-finite floats are null (JSON-safe). If no data / no factor evaluates, the payload is {"failure": "NO_DATA" | "NO_FACTORS", "detail": "..."} (HTTP 200); an invalid knob (bad method / standardize / out-of-range field) is HTTP 422. SDK from assay.service import AssayService from assay.config import AssayConfig svc = AssayService(AssayConfig()) out = svc.combine_factors( ["rank(close)", "alpha101:1", "lib:<id>"], train=("2025-01-02", "2025-10-31"), val=("2025-11-01", "2026-01-31"), test=("2026-02-01", "2026-06-09"), universe="NASDAQ100", horizons=[1, 5, 10], method="auto", # or any name from combination_methods() # method="lightgbm", model_params={"n_estimators": 500}, ) print(out["method"], out["test"]["ic"], out["test"]["icir"]) print(svc.combination_methods()) # [{name, kind, available}, ...] The pure-numpy kernel (engine-free, reusable in isolation) is assay.evaluator.combine_factors(...) , which returns a CombinationResult whose .combined is the (T, N) composite signal. Notes & caveats Data window. The bundled US data covers a specific range — pass split windows inside it (the WebUI auto-fills them from the ingested range; CLI/SDK do not). auto candidate set defaults to the cheap analytic schemes. To let auto also try models, pass candidate_methods=[...] including model names. Threading. Tree/boosting models are fit with a bounded worker count — the pooled design is small, and unbounded n_jobs=-1 oversubscribes OpenMP on many-core hosts. Backtesting the composite. The composite is a learned signal , not an expression, so it does not yet feed directly into the portfolio backtester (which takes an expression). The (T, N) composite is available on the kernel result for custom downstream use.

title: Portfolio Backtest
text: Portfolio Backtest Turn a factor signal into a simulated portfolio with real trading constraints and costs, and get a PortfolioReport (Sharpe, drawdown, turnover, cost drag, NAV series). Design spec: portfolio-backtest.md . Quick start import assay from assay.portfolio import PortfolioBacktestConfig cfg = PortfolioBacktestConfig( universe="NASDAQ100", period_start="2025-01-02", period_end="2026-06-09", market="US", rebalance_type="monthly", # daily|weekly|monthly|quarterly|threshold|signal weight_method="signal_prop", # equal|signal_prop|quintile|decile|mv|bl|risk_parity long_short=False, max_single_weight=0.05, execution_price="next_open", # next_open|next_close ) pf = assay.backtest_portfolio("cs_rank(ts_returns(close, 20))", cfg) print(pf.total_return, pf.annual_return, pf.sharpe, pf.max_drawdown, pf.annual_turnover, pf.cost_drag, pf.n_rebalances) pf.to_dict() # JSON-safe, agent-ready CLI: python -m assay.cli portfolio 'cs_rank(ts_returns(close, 20))' \ --start 2025-01-02 --end 2026-06-09 --rebalance monthly --weight-method signal_prop REST: POST /v1/portfolio/backtest (see the REST guide ). Long/short, dollar-neutral cfg = PortfolioBacktestConfig( universe="NASDAQ100", period_start="2025-01-02", period_end="2026-06-09", weight_method="quintile", long_short=True, net_exposure=0.0, # dollar-neutral quintile_long_n=1, quintile_short_n=1, ) pf = assay.backtest_portfolio("cs_rank(ts_corr(close, volume, 20))", cfg) Weight methods Method Notes equal equal weight across the eligible set signal_prop proportional to the (normalized) signal quintile / decile top/bottom buckets long/short mv mean-variance via OSQP and Clarabel (scipy SLSQP if OSQP is not installed) + numpy Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage (no cvxpy/sklearn) risk_parity inverse-vol / equal-risk-contribution (long-only) Key config groups rebalance_* (schedule + min_rebalance_interval , execution_offset_days ), weights ( gross_exposure , net_exposure , signal_transform ), constraints ( max_single_weight , max/min_stock_count , max_turnover_per_period ), execution ( slippage_model , slippage_k , max_adv_fraction , partial_fill_handling ), benchmark ( benchmark , risk_free_rate ), output ( save_trade_log , save_position_log ). PortfolioBacktestConfig.preset('US'|'A'|'HK') applies market cost/limit defaults. Full field list: the design doc §2. Metrics in the report Returns (total/annual/gross/excess), risk-adjusted (Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, information ratio, max drawdown + recovery, beta, CAPM alpha, tracking error), turnover & cost (annual turnover, cost drag, avg holding days), plus nav_series / nav_dates , monthly_returns , trade_log , position_log , and a_share_metrics (only when market='A' ). A-share Set market="A" (or PortfolioBacktestConfig.preset("A") ) to activate T+1 settlement, price-limit blocking, and the stamp-duty/commission/transfer-fee cost model. These run on any market's data when their inputs are supplied ( prev_close for price limits, a tradable_mask for ST/suspension, etc.). On US data the data-dependent filters are inert (no crash). A true index benchmark needs an index price series Assay doesn't have — the benchmark is an equal-weight-universe proxy. Caveats on the current dataset Unadjusted splits. If the data folder has no adj_events , a few real splits show up as ~−90% single-day returns that inflate results. Backfill corporate actions ( assay.cli corp-actions ) to get clean numbers — see the data pipeline guide . rebalance_type='signal' with a high-autocorrelation factor may never fire (spec-compliant), leaving a flat all-cash NAV — choose a calendar schedule for a non-degenerate run.

title: Precompute & Common Sub-Expression Elimination (CSE)
headings: Coupled to the daily data update
Use it to accelerate a sweep
text: Precompute & Common Sub-Expression Elimination (CSE) When you evaluate many factors over the same panel — a sweep, a library re-score, a combination search — they share sub-expressions. Sub(high, low) , Mean(volume, 20) , Ref(close, 1) recur in thousands of otherwise-distinct factors. Computing each shared subtree once and reusing the result is the single biggest lever on batch throughput. Assay does this two ways, both keyed off the AST's stable struct_hash : two structurally identical subtrees — regardless of which surface syntax produced them — share a hash and are computed once. In-process CSE — FactorEngine.evaluate_many([...]) threads one structural-hash memo across every expression, so a subtree shared across the batch is evaluated exactly once. Zero setup, always correct. Persistent precompute — PrecomputeStore mines the corpus's hottest subtrees, materialises each one for every asset , and stores the (T, N) matrix on disk. Subsequent batches load those subtrees instead of recomputing them — across runs and processes . Both are bit-for-bit identical to per-factor evaluate() (verified: max|Δ| = 0 , identical NaN pattern). Measured A 1,200-factor sample from the sweep corpus over a 400×150 panel (structural sharing ratio 2.3×): Path Throughput Speedup naive per-factor evaluate() 5 factors/s base evaluate_many() (in-process CSE) 6 factors/s 1.20× evaluate_many(precompute=…) warm 6 factors/s 1.18× The in-process CSE speedup scales with how much the corpus overlaps — a random 1,200-factor sample shares less than the full 15k corpus, where the hottest subtrees recur thousands of times ( sub(high, low) ×4,667). The persistent precompute pays off across repeated sweeps over a stable panel (build once at ~1s; reuse across runs and processes) and when expensive subtrees recur; for a single sweep whose shared subtrees are cheap it is roughly neutral (disk load ≈ recompute). Pick the tool to the workload — see the table at the end. Find the common sub-expressions # pure analysis — no data needed python -m assay.cli precompute top --corpus _assay_sweep/factors_canonical_unique.txt --top-k 15 top 15 common sub-expressions in _assay_sweep/factors_canonical_unique.txt: x4667 nodes=3 score=9334 sub(high, low) x1872 nodes=3 score=3744 ts_delay(close, 1) x1563 nodes=3 score=3126 ts_mean(volume, 20) x1351 nodes=3 score=2702 ts_std(close, 20) ... count — total occurrences across the corpus. score — count × (n_nodes − 1) , the operator-evaluations saved by computing the subtree once and reusing it everywhere (the ranking key). SDK: service.common_subexpressions(corpus, top_k=100) → [{expr, count, n_factors, n_nodes, score}] . Build the precompute store python -m assay.cli precompute build \ --corpus _assay_sweep/factors_canonical_unique.txt \ --universe NASDAQ100 --start 2025-01-02 --end 2026-06-09 --top-k 512 python -m assay.cli precompute stats This mines the top- k shared subtrees and computes each one for all assets , storing the matrices under <data_dir>/precompute/ . Building is itself CSE-accelerated (nested shared subtrees compute once). SDK: import assay svc = assay.init() info = svc.build_precompute( "_assay_sweep/factors_canonical_unique.txt", universe="NASDAQ100", period=("2025-01-02", "2026-06-09"), top_k=512, ) print(info["built"], "subexprs |", info["est_evals_saved"], "evals saved / pass") Auto-update by history The on-disk key folds in FactorEngine.panel_fingerprint() — a digest of the panel's dates × symbols × fields . Ingest new history and the fingerprint changes, so stale entries simply stop matching (a miss) and the store rebuilds for the new panel. No manual invalidation; entries are stable and shared within a panel. Coupled to the daily data update The hot cache is wired into the data pipeline so it stays aligned with the live data automatically : After a successful data-update job ( POST /v1/admin/data/jobs ), the same job refreshes the precompute store for that market's primary universe, over the freshly-ingested data range , mining the factor library as the corpus ( AssayService.refresh_precompute_for_market ). An init run refreshes every universe. Each build writes a manifest recording its validity period, as_of , fingerprint, build time and the latest ingested date — so freshness is a cheap date comparison (no panel load). The data manager page (Admin → Data Manager) shows a Hot cache card: per universe, the validity period, entry count, top sub-expressions, and a fresh / stale badge (stale = the data advanced since the cache was built). A Rebuild US / Rebuild CN button queues a full rebuild of every universe. GET /v1/admin/cache/status -> {store:{entries,bytes,dir}, scopes:[{universe, period, as_of, fingerprint, built_at, data_latest, n_entries, fresh, top}]} POST /v1/admin/cache/rebuild {market} -> queues a background rebuild job precompute_status() marks a scope fresh only when its recorded data_latest still equals the market's current latest ingested date — i.e. the cache is aligned to the live data validity period. Use it to accelerate a sweep # raw factor VALUES for a big corpus, CSE + precompute accelerated results = svc.evaluate_many(exprs, universe="NASDAQ100", period=("2025-01-02", "2026-06-09"), use_precompute=True) for r in results: # r is a FactorResult: r.values is the (T, N) matrix ... At the engine level (no service / data layer): from assay.engine import FactorEngine, PrecomputeStore eng = FactorEngine(panel) store = PrecomputeStore("/path/to/precompute") store.build(eng, corpus_exprs, top_k=512) # once bound = store.bind(eng.panel_fingerprint()) results = eng.evaluate_many(exprs, precompute=bound) # warm: hot subtrees loaded, not recomputed print(f"{bound.hit_rate:.0%} of subtree lookups served from precompute") evaluate_many returns one FactorResult per input (values only — no IC metrics). A malformed expression raises, exactly like evaluate() ; pre-filter with engine.diagnose() if you need soft failures. When to use which Situation Use One factor evaluate() A batch, occasional evaluate_many() (in-process CSE — free) Repeated sweeps over a stable panel precompute build once, then evaluate_many(..., use_precompute=True) Scoring (IC / decay / turnover), not raw values batch() (per-factor metrics) How it works (internals) assay.engine.cse.common_subexpressions(exprs) — parse the corpus, walk every AST, aggregate subtrees by struct_hash , rank by recompute saved. FactorEngine._eval_cse(node, ctx, memo, precompute) — memoised evaluation: each OpNode result is cached by its struct_hash ; a bound precompute short-circuits a subtree by loading its matrix from disk. Leaves (fields / literals) cost nothing and are never cached. PrecomputeStore — content-addressed (hash, fingerprint) → (T, N).npy , sharded and written atomically (temp file + os.replace ), best-effort (a corrupt file reads as a miss). Mirrors the L2 factor cache. Correctness rests on operator purity : kernels return new arrays and never mutate inputs, so sharing one array object across many parents is safe — the same assumption the engine already makes when it reuses a field matrix across every reference within a single evaluation.

title: Performance & Caching
text: Performance & Caching The default local-data research backend reuses market panels and factor values across experiments. Each experiment still runs its diagnostics and portfolio evaluation and writes its own persistent research record. Research execution reuse Layer Reused work Invalidation and limits Panel and engine pool Loaded prices, field matrices, membership, groups and forward returns Store, universe, period, as-of date, adjustment and source-file revision; up to 4 idle retained contexts and an estimated 256 MiB retained-memory budget Subexpression memo Raw built-in operator results shared by factor expressions Per engine, bounded to 32 MiB; operator replacement clears the memo L2 factor values Computed factor matrices across process restarts Observed panel fingerprint, expression, operator signature and implementation digest; atomic disk publication The memory estimate includes panels, engine/session arrays, additional forward-return horizons and the reserved memo capacity. Active leases can temporarily exceed the retention budget; idle entries are evicted when a lease finishes. Calls sharing one engine are serialized, while different retained panels can be evaluated concurrently. Subexpressions are cached before output membership masking, so rolling operators retain history from before a security joined the universe. Custom or replaced operators bypass factor-value caching. Portfolio reports and research records are recomputed independently. New request IDs consume the research budget even when the expression is cached; retrying an existing request ID preserves the original attempt. This path applies to the native DataStore through the research backend, including its REST, MCP and SDK entry points. Custom stores and QFVPanelStore retain their existing execution behavior. A direct call to AssayService.evaluate does not acquire this pool; explicit sessions and the standalone L2 cache remain available separately. Source updates Reuse supports read-only market data or the canonical ingester's atomic file replacement. File revision checks cover prices, membership, adjustments, groups and trade status and run again after loading or waiting for an engine. A change during these checks fails the attempt so it can be retried with a fresh panel. The revision token uses file metadata, not a content scan on every request. External writers that modify files in place while preserving metadata must disable panel reuse: from assay.research import AssayBackend service.research.backends["assay"] = AssayBackend(service, reuse_panels=False) The pool does not create a transactional snapshot of a dataset being updated concurrently. Use a stable published dataset revision for reproducible experiments. Inspect reuse backend = service.research.backends["assay"] print(backend.execution_pool.stats()) # panel_hits, panel_builds, evictions, entries, retained_bytes, # factor_computations, factor_disk_hits, subtree_hits Hit and build counters span the pool lifetime. Factor counters describe currently retained entries and reset when those entries are evicted. Alpha-101 cache microbenchmark The standalone Alpha-101 benchmark remains available for synthetic and real panels: PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/bench_alpha101.py --synthetic --n 200 --t 504 PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/bench_alpha101.py --real --start 2025-01-02 --end 2026-06-09 PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -m performance -s It checks cache/no-cache matrix equality. Its disk-hit timing excludes the diagnostics, portfolio construction and persistence included in a complete research attempt. Background: cache design and precomputation and CSE .

title: REST API
text: REST API FastAPI app exposing AssayService over HTTP, with SSE streaming for evaluation. Run it: python -m assay.cli serve-api --port 8000 # or: uvicorn assay.api.app:app --port 8000 Public base: https://assay.qfinverse.com · local base: http://localhost:8000 Interactive docs (Swagger): http://localhost:8000/docs The WebUI is served at / (see the WebUI guide ). Production configuration, proxying, readiness and release checks: deployment . MCP shares this app at /mcp/ . Durable research endpoints All routes below use the same workspace as MCP and require the configured API credentials. Method Path under /v1/research Purpose GET /backends Declared backends; optional read-only probe=true GET / POST /datasets List / register evaluation specifications GET / POST /sessions Discover / create research sessions POST /sessions/import Import a verified session manifest GET /sessions/{id} · /manifest · /context State, export and compact context GET /sessions/{id}/audit Read-only judge packet; offset , limit , expected_manifest_hash POST /sessions/{id}/experiments · /notes Evaluate an attempt / append a note GET / POST /sessions/{id}/checkpoints List checkpoint streams / save a version with compare-and-set GET /sessions/{id}/checkpoints/{name} Restore a checkpoint and inspect intervening attempts GET / POST /programs Discover / create a multi-window research program POST /programs/import Atomically restore a program manifest GET /programs/{id}/manifest Export the program with its sessions and links GET /programs/{id} · /factors/{factor_id} Inspect linked sessions / factor history GET /programs/{id}/candidates Canonical factor pool with session-scoped decisions POST /programs/{id}/sessions · /reassessments Link a session / evaluate a factor on another window POST /programs/{id}/window-comparisons Descriptive RankIC change across compatible non-overlapping windows GET /experiments/{id} Summary or paginated section , offset , limit POST /experiments/compare Compare at least two attempts POST /experiments/{id}/replay · /reconcile · /cancel · /abandon Explicit execution recovery POST /experiments/{id}/decisions Record a candidate decision GET /sessions/{id}/candidates Candidate states GET /factors/{id}/history Paginated lifecycle history, offset / limit OpenAPI contains the full request schemas. Experiment request IDs are required; repeat them after a timeout to retrieve the same attempt without spending another budget unit. Research records are shared among authenticated researchers. Auth A server runs in one of three modes: Mode Set Callers identify with Open nothing nothing — every request is allowed (local use) Service keys ASSAY_API_KEYS (comma-separated), optionally ASSAY_ADMIN_KEYS X-API-Key header Accounts ASSAY_ACCOUNTS=1 the browser session, or a personal key in X-API-Key With accounts on (as on assay.qfinverse.com), people join by invitation, sign in at /login , and create personal keys ( asy_... ) on the Account page. A key acts as its owner and is shown once. Send it as X-API-Key (or Authorization: Bearer ). Service keys keep working next to accounts. Admin routes ( /v1/admin/* , /auth/users , /auth/invites ) need an admin account or an admin service key. export ASSAY_KEY=asy_... # from the Account page curl -s -H "X-API-Key: $ASSAY_KEY" https://assay.qfinverse.com/v1/system/universes Account endpoints Method Path Purpose GET /auth/status · /auth/me Server mode; who is signed in POST /auth/login · /auth/logout Start / end a browser session POST /auth/register · /auth/reset-password Sign up with an invitation; set a password from a reset link POST /auth/password · PATCH /auth/profile Change own password / name GET/POST/DELETE /auth/keys Own API keys (create from a signed-in browser only) GET/PATCH/DELETE /auth/users Admins: users, roles, disabling POST /auth/users/{id}/reset Admins: one-time password reset link GET/POST/DELETE /auth/invites Admins: invitations (role, uses, expiry) Endpoints Method Path Purpose GET /health Liveness POST /v1/factor/evaluate Evaluate one factor — JSON report, or SSE stream when stream:true POST /v1/factor/batch Batch evaluate → {total, elapsed_ms, reports} POST /v1/factor/lint Parse-only: {dialect, canonical, fields, operators, ast, diagnostics} (no data) GET /v1/library/factors List with filters ( min_rank_icir , source , sort_by , limit , ...) GET /v1/library/factors/{id} Full FactorReport POST /v1/library/factors Save a report DELETE /v1/library/factors Delete by {factor_ids: [...]} GET /v1/library/correlation-matrix Pairwise correlation for factor_ids GET /v1/library/ic-heatmap · /embedding · /lineage RankIC-over-time, 2-D similarity map, derivation DAG POST /v1/library/factors/bulk Bulk-evaluate + save expressions POST /v1/library/prune Identify/remove redundant factors GET /v1/combination/methods List combination schemes (learned models flagged available) POST /v1/combination Combine factors, score train/val/test → composite + model POST/GET/DELETE /v1/combination/saved Save / list / delete saved combination runs GET /v1/combination/saved/{id} Reload one saved run (the fitted model) GET /v1/market/bars OHLCV bars for one symbol ( freq , adj ) POST /v1/market/factor-series One factor's value for one symbol over time POST /v1/session/create · DELETE /v1/session/{id} Create / release a panel-cached session POST /v1/portfolio/backtest Run a portfolio backtest → PortfolioReport GET /v1/system/status · /universes · /data-calendar Engine/data/cache status, universes, coverage — Data manager ( /v1/admin/* , operator) see below Data-manager (admin) endpoints Operator surface behind the WebUI Data tab (hidden from the OpenAPI schema, but live): Method Path Purpose GET/PUT /v1/admin/config Read (masked) / update dirs, credentials, system settings GET /v1/admin/data/status · /usage RAW↔ASSAY sync snapshot · per-market disk sizes (RAW + ASSAY) POST /v1/admin/data/test Test a provider connection ( {provider: massive|tushare} ) POST /v1/admin/data/jobs Queue a job ( mode: init|update|ingest ); GET list; GET /{id} one GET/PUT /v1/admin/schedule Auto-update schedule (per market: enabled + daily time) GET /v1/admin/cache/status · /entries · POST /rebuild Hot-cache status / contents / rebuild Evaluate — blocking curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/factor/evaluate \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"expr":"ts_corr(close, volume, 20)","universe":"NASDAQ100", "period":["2025-01-02","2026-06-09"],"horizons":[1,5,10,20]}' # -> { ...FactorReport } Evaluate — SSE stream Set "stream": true ; the response is text/event-stream with frames: event: eval.started data: {"factor_id": "...", "expr": "..."} event: eval.ic_series data: {"ic": [...], "rank_ic": [...], "dates": [...]} event: eval.decay data: {"ic_by_horizon": {...}, "halflife": 12} event: eval.groups data: {"quintile_returns": [...]} event: eval.complete data: { ...full FactorReport } All data is NaN-safe JSON (NaN/Inf → null), so JSON.parse never fails. EventSource can't POST — consume the stream with fetch + a ReadableStream reader (the WebUI does this). Portfolio backtest curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/portfolio/backtest \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"expr":"cs_rank(ts_returns(close, 20))", "config":{"universe":"NASDAQ100","period_start":"2025-01-02","period_end":"2026-06-09", "rebalance_type":"monthly","weight_method":"signal_prop"}}' Error schema Errors mirror the engine diagnostics ( assay.engine.diagnostics ): stable code ( ASSAY-P###/E###/O### ), failure_mode ( SYNTAX_ERROR · LOOKAHEAD · CONSTANT · ALL_NAN · RUNTIME_ERROR ), severity , stage , message , location , suggestion . A request that needs ingested data returns 503 when the store is empty. Full contract: architecture.md §4.

title: Python SDK
text: Python SDK The SDK ( import assay ) is the lowest-latency surface — in-process, no serialization. It auto-initializes from the environment on first use. import assay assay.init() # optional; reads AssayConfig.from_env(); backtest() auto-inits otherwise Public surface ( assay.__all__ ): init , backtest , batch_backtest , backtest_portfolio , stream , Session , library , plus AssayConfig , MassiveConfig , AssayService . Single-factor evaluation report = assay.backtest( "ts_corr(close, volume, 20)", universe = "NASDAQ100", period = ("2025-01-02", "2026-06-09"), horizons = [1, 5, 10, 20], execution = "next_open", # next_open | next_close (no vwap) neutralize = None, # ["sector"] needs group data (absent for US) as_of = "2026-06-09", # PIT: only data known by this date adj = "split", # none | split | total ) report.rank_ic, report.rank_icir # headline IC report.ic_by_horizon # {1: .., 5: .., ...} report.decay_halflife_days report.turnover_1d, report.redundancy_score report.lookahead_detected, report.failure_mode, report.suggestion report.diagnostics # structured ASSAY-* diagnostics on failure/warning report.to_dict(); report.to_json(); report.to_dataframe() # JSON-safe / IC time series Expressions accept both syntaxes (they lower to the same AST): assay.backtest("Corr($close, $volume, 20)") # qlib assay.backtest("ts_corr(close, volume, 20)") # function-call / Alpha-101 Batch evaluation factors = ["ts_returns(close, 20)", "ts_corr(close, volume, 20)", "cs_rank(ts_std(close, 20))"] reports = assay.batch_backtest(factors, universe="NASDAQ100", period=("2025-01-02", "2026-06-09"), sort_by="rank_icir") for r in reports[:5]: print(f"{r.expr:<40} ICIR={r.rank_icir:.2f}") Sessions (amortize panel load) A session loads the price panel and forward returns once; subsequent factors reuse them. with assay.Session(universe="NASDAQ100", period=("2025-01-02", "2026-06-09")) as sess: r1 = sess.backtest("ts_returns(close, 20)") # loads the panel r2 = sess.backtest("ts_corr(close, volume, 20)") # reuses it (much faster) reports = sess.batch_backtest(factors) Streaming (async) import asyncio async def watch(): async for ev in assay.stream("ts_corr(close, volume, 20)", universe="NASDAQ100"): if ev["event"] == "eval.complete": print(ev["data"]["rank_icir"]) asyncio.run(watch()) Events arrive in order: eval.started , eval.ic_series , eval.decay , eval.groups , eval.complete (with the full report). All frames are NaN-safe JSON. Factor library assay.library.save(report) factors = assay.library.list(min_rank_icir=0.5, sort_by="rank_icir", limit=20) r = assay.library.get(factor_id) corr = assay.library.correlation_matrix([f.factor_id for f in factors]) assay.library.prune(threshold=0.7, dry_run=True) assay.library.delete([factor_id]) Portfolio backtest from assay.portfolio import PortfolioBacktestConfig cfg = PortfolioBacktestConfig(universe="NASDAQ100", period_start="2025-01-02", period_end="2026-06-09", market="US", rebalance_type="monthly", weight_method="signal_prop", long_short=False) pf = assay.backtest_portfolio("cs_rank(ts_returns(close, 20))", cfg) print(pf.sharpe, pf.max_drawdown, pf.annual_turnover, pf.cost_drag, pf.n_rebalances) backtest_portfolio(expr, config=None, **config_kwargs) — pass a PortfolioBacktestConfig or keyword fields. See the portfolio guide . Custom config from assay.config import AssayConfig svc = assay.init(AssayConfig.from_env()) # or AssayConfig.for_tests(tmp_dir) offline

title: MCP Server
text: MCP Server The source server has 53 tools , including eight FactorDB tools and 34 research tools for datasets, sessions, experiments, search checkpoints and programs. The deployed service can run a different version. See the agent research guide . assay_research_audit returns read-only, evidence-linked checks for a human or agent judge. See research audit for its scope, paging and snapshot pinning. The MCP server exposes Assay's evaluate→library loop as Model Context Protocol tools that LLM agents call to drive autonomous alpha mining. Built on the high-level FastMCP API ( src/assay/mcp/server.py ). Public endpoint Connect remote agents to https://assay.qfinverse.com/mcp/ using Streamable HTTP. Send a personal/service key as Authorization: Bearer … or X-API-Key . The model provider key and Assay's access key are separate credentials. This deployment does not implement OAuth; the client must support sending these headers. Connection metadata is available at /.well-known/assay.json . It reports the deployed tool count and schema digest. Research sessions persist in the server database; MCP transport sessions themselves are stateless. import asyncio import os from assay.mcp.client import connect_mcp async def main(): async with connect_mcp(url="https://assay.qfinverse.com/mcp/", api_key=os.environ["ASSAY_MCP_API_KEY"]) as session: tools = await session.list_tools() print([tool.name for tool in tools.tools]) print(await session.call_tool("assay_backend_list", {"probe": True})) asyncio.run(main()) For research, use dataset → research session → experiment → inspection/decision. assay_experiment_run uses default panel/factor reuse and records each attempt. Use compact context and paginated experiment/history reads for routine inspection. The immediate run/replay result still includes the full saved attempt for compatibility. Authenticated researchers currently share one workspace. Deployment and post-release checks: deployment guide . Local execution python -m assay.mcp.server # stdio (Claude Desktop / local agents) python -m assay.cli serve-mcp --transport http --port 8001 # shared authenticated HTTP app Install .[api,mcp] for HTTP mode. Stdio remains available with the MCP extra alone. Prepared local market data requires no vendor credentials. Legacy --transport sse is restricted to loopback development; public deployments use the shared HTTP app. Evaluation and library tools (11) Tool Purpose assay_evaluate Evaluate one factor → FactorReport (qlib or Python syntax) assay_batch Evaluate many factors in parallel, sorted by rank_icir (prefer over a loop) assay_lint Data-free syntax check of an expression (dialect, fields, operators, diagnostics) assay_universes List available universes with symbol counts and default assay_portfolio_backtest Full portfolio backtest of a factor → compact PortfolioReport assay_library_list List library factors with filters (check redundancy before generating) assay_library_get Full FactorReport for one factor assay_library_save Save a report to the library assay_library_correlation Pairwise correlation between factor IDs assay_library_prune Identify / remove redundant factors assay_system_status Data freshness + cache statistics assay_evaluate 's description is enriched at runtime with the live operator schema ( assay.engine.operator_schema() ), so agents see the available operators inline. Claude Desktop config ~/.config/claude/claude_desktop_config.json : { "mcpServers": { "assay": { "command": "python", "args": ["-m", "assay.mcp.server"], "env": { "ASSAY_DATA_DIR": "data_2025_2026h1" } } } } Typical agent loop Design contract: architecture.md §6.

title: Integrated Assay architecture
text: Integrated Assay architecture This document describes the current local architecture and retains historical integration evidence. See the project overview for the distinction between local and deployed versions. Assay combines the upstream factor computation platform with a persistent research workspace. Both live in this repository; QFinVerse is an optional data producer, not a service that must be installed for the offline research workflow. Complete capability map Data and computation: prepared US/CN/HK data and an optional QFinVerse daily panel, Python/qlib expression syntax, a shared AST, factor scoring, diagnostics, factor combinations, and portfolio backtests. Shared factor infrastructure: FactorDB identities, deduplication, values, novelty queries, and batch jobs; optional ADES controllers and workers execute job slices with leases and heartbeats. Persistent research: dataset specifications, goals, attempt budgets, successful/failed experiments, revisions, notes, context, explicit replay, and integrity-checked export/import. Agent access: 53 MCP tools, a replaceable reference client with request/tool limits and raw receipts, SDK and REST. The agent supplies the research policy. Human access: the four-area workbench in the integrated sidebar, accounts and keys, Doc Hub, and existing factor and portfolio pages. Task Entry points Records Individual evaluation/diagnosis assay_evaluate , assay_lint , /v1/factor/* FactorReport and existing factor library Persistent hypothesis testing assay_research_* , assay_experiment_* , /v1/research/* Session, independent attempts, notes, manifests Shared batch computation fdb_submit , fdb_job , fdb_query , /v1/fdb/* FactorDB factors, specs, jobs Distributed FactorDB execution /v1/ades/* and worker processes Leased slices and results Human inspection/intervention /#/research , console pages, /doc/ The same research records as SDK/MCP A session workflow registers a dataset, creates a goal, inspects context, evaluates candidates, retains failures, links revisions, writes notes and exports records. The FactorDB submit/job/query workflow can use ADES but does not automatically produce those session records. Selecting the factordb_ades research backend links a session attempt to a durable FactorDB job and its versioned result receipt. Responsibilities Component Responsibility Retained implementation Factor engine and portfolio evaluation Parse expressions, compute panels, score factors, simulate portfolios Upstream engine, vectorized operations, optional Rust kernels and OSQP/Clarabel solvers Factor infrastructure Canonical factor identities, stored values, novelty queries, asynchronous jobs Upstream FactorDB and its eight MCP operations; private accounts use separate registries Distributed execution Lease factor-computation slices to workers Upstream ADES controller, worker, heartbeat and task queue Research workspace Dataset specifications, goals, attempt budgets, hypotheses, failed evaluations, parent links, notes, manifests Persistent SQLite workspace and backend protocol Agent and human clients Choose research actions, inspect outcomes and continue sessions Reference agent, 34 research MCP operations, SDK/REST and browser workbench Application shell Authentication, navigation and documentation Upstream account/session authentication and sidebar, with the research page added The MCP server has 53 operations: 11 evaluation/library tools, eight FactorDB tools, and 34 research tools. HTTP MCP is mounted at /mcp/ ; each API application owns an independent HTTP lifecycle. Stdio remains available for local agent clients. Distinct records and budgets A FactorDB factor is a canonical expression and its computed evidence. Service keys use a shared workspace, while private accounts use separate registries. A research attempt records one session decision, including failure and provenance. Repeated attempts remain separate records even when their expressions match. The existing factor library remains available as well. Integrating the modules does not silently merge their schemas or delete historical records. The default research backend calls the in-process evaluator. The opt-in factordb_ades backend submits the same research attempt to FactorDB/ADES and stores its job ID, factor ID, spec, owner and logical data version. Call assay_experiment_reconcile after a timeout or restart; repeated reconciliation preserves submission identity and spends no additional attempt budget. Queue completion/final failure receipts survive interruption before registry updates; registry application records progress and compute usage once per task. The workspace separately enforces a per-session attempt budget. FactorDB daily compute usage is charged on the receipt's UTC completion day. With account authentication enabled, private tasks are attributed to the account; service keys retain the shared service workspace. This budget is not a reservation of future compute or a hard CPU, memory, or storage quota. Persistent research sessions differ from temporary evaluator panel sessions. Reconciliation recovers asynchronous execution evidence; it does not restart a worker or restore a model conversation. Synchronous interrupted attempts still require inspection and explicit abandonment. Live asynchronous attempts cannot be abandoned; cancellation uses assay_experiment_cancel with a saved reason. Cancellation fences leases and delayed dispatch, and rejects late results; it does not interrupt native computation already running on a remote worker. Accepted completion wins a race with cancellation. The attempt charge remains consumed. See the asynchronous recipe in Agent research . Authentication and data Research REST routes use the existing get_api_key dependency, inheriting service keys, personal API keys, account cookies and same-origin mutation checks. The local implementation provides private per-account research stores when account authentication is enabled; service keys retain the shared workspace. Market data, the ADES queue and trusted workers can still be shared. The current deployed version uses a shared research workspace. Manual browser writes remain labeled human:webui . The built-in data store and upstream QFinVerse-panel reader are retained. Local synthetic and prepared data remain usable without a QFinVerse installation. Dataset specification hashes identify configuration, not immutable physical data. Integration provenance The preserved local research implementation is commit 871a961 ; the upstream baseline is 103532807af5fdcbf8748d081ca953bf430a35be . A backup branch, codex/pre-upstream-integration-20261108 , retains the complete local state before integration. The integration branch is codex/integrate-upstream-20261108 . Historical model studies retain their original source snapshots, plans and receipts. Integration does not rewrite their results or imply that the studies evaluated FactorDB, ADES or the new HTTP endpoint. New live studies must freeze the integrated source as a new inventory. Integration checks and the independent audit are retained under artifacts/upstream-integration-20261108/ . Validation and paper scope The integrated suite reports 1,146 passing tests, three skips and zero failures. Two optional unbuilt Rust test modules and one optional scikit-learn test are skipped; native throughput and production performance gains are not reported. The real browser regression covers failure, revision, notes, original manifest bytes, fresh-workspace import and reload, separately from transport-race fixtures. An installed wheel is checked outside the repository, including actual HTTP MCP. The earlier model evidence contains 24 tasks, four configurations and three model families, each task completing two new evaluations. These inventories use earlier frozen sources and do not evaluate FactorDB, ADES or the integrated HTTP service. The system paper describes component boundaries, inspectable workflows and this versioned evidence. Real-task benefits, researcher time savings, deployment and framework comparisons remain unmeasured. Further state ablations are optional analysis, rather than a default prerequisite for a system paper. The subsequent asynchronous bridge passes 1,160 tests with three optional skips; real-worker and fault-injection checks are retained under artifacts/async-research-20261108/ . The cancellation extension passes 1,177 tests with three optional skips. Evidence is retained under artifacts/research-cancellation-20261108/ . Discarded in-flight worker compute is not measured by accepted-result usage accounting.

title: FactorDB — a factor store for large-scale, agent-driven research
headings: 2. Core idea: compute once on a global grid
text: FactorDB — a factor store for large-scale, agent-driven research With account authentication, personal FactorDB jobs and scores use private registries; the shared service registry remains available to the service key. ADES workers are trusted and can read the expressions they execute. Status: design + phase 1 (daily) implementation. Scope: Assay on the QFinVerse daily panel (US), extended to minute bars in phase 2. 1. Why Assay today evaluates a factor by loading a (dates × symbols) panel for one universe and period, walking the expression, and scoring it. Results are cached by (expression, universe, period, adjustment) . That works for one researcher; it does not work for hundreds of agents proposing tens of thousands of factors: Problem Effect Results keyed by universe and period ts_mean(volume, 20) on SP500 2016–2026 is recomputed for NASDAQ100, for 2018–2026, and for every agent One process, one panel per request no use of 32 cores; a TOP3000 batch is CPU-bound in one thread float64 everywhere twice the memory of the source data (float32) Warm-up NaNs at the window start a 60-day window loses 60 days at the start of every request Agent tools mirror the human API one blocking call per factor, large payloads, no dedup across agents, no budget 2. Core idea: compute once on a global grid Every factor expression splits into two kinds of work: Column-separable work — time-series and element-wise operators ( ts_* , + - * / , log , where , …). The value for security s on date t depends only on s 's own history up to t . It does not depend on the universe. Row-coupled work — cross-sectional operators ( cs_rank , cs_zscore , cs_neutralize , group operators). The value depends on which securities are in the cross-section that day. FactorDB stores the column-separable part once, on a global grid : every trading day of the store × every security that was ever a member of the widest universe (TOP3000 ∪ index members). A request for any universe and period slices rows and columns out of that grid, then applies the row-coupled operators for that universe on the fly. Cross-sectional work is a single pass per date and is cheap next to rolling windows. cs_rank( ts_corr(close, volume, 20) ) └──── stored on the grid ────┘ computed per request, on the universe's members Expressions whose time-series operators sit above a cross-sectional one ( ts_mean(cs_rank(x), 5) ) depend on the universe; their nodes are stored per universe (the grid key includes the universe) and still shared across periods and agents. 2.1 Canonical form and identity Before anything is computed an expression is parsed and canonicalised: commutative operators ( add , mul , elem_min , elem_max , eq , ne , and , or ) sort their arguments, numeric literals are normalised, and windows are floored as the engine does. The structural hash of the canonical tree is the factor id . Two agents that write close/open and div(close, open) get the same id; submitting a known id costs nothing. 2.2 Node store Each stored node is a float32 matrix on the grid, split into year blocks ( nodes/<hash>/<year>.npy , memory-mapped). Year blocks make appends cheap (only the current year is rewritten) and reads fast (a 2016–2026 slice touches 11 files, each read by mmap). Each year block is security-major ( n_sids × days ): a worker that computes a slice of securities writes contiguous ranges, and a universe read takes one contiguous run per security. (A day-major block made every 25-column write touch every page of the file, which on the 15 GB production box meant gigabytes of read-modify-write per task.) A manifest row per node records the canonical expression, the grid, the dates it covers, bytes, compute cost and hit counts (used for eviction and for agents' "is this already known" queries). What gets stored: the frontier of each factor: the largest column-separable subtrees (the inputs of the first cross-sectional operator, or the whole factor if it has none); any column-separable subtree used by two or more factors in the store (popularity is counted per node). Leaf fields are not copied; they are read from the QFinVerse panel's own year blocks. 2.3 Corporate actions and point-in-time correctness The QFinVerse panel stores prices as traded and adjusts on read onto the basis of the window's last day. FactorDB computes grid nodes on the basis of the store's last day E . A request that ends at E′ < E must see values on E′ 's basis. For a node that is homogeneous in prices the two differ by a per-security constant: each field has a degree under splits and under dividends: close/open/high/low = (1, 1), volume = (−1, 0), transactions , dvol , ret = (0, 0); operators combine degrees ( mul adds, div subtracts, add/sub/min/max/where need equal degrees, ts_mean/ts_sum/ts_std/ts_delay/ts_min/ts_max/abs/neg keep the degree, ts_corr/ts_rank/ts_returns/cs_*/sign/comparisons give (0, 0), log/sqrt/pow of a non-zero degree have none); a node with degree (a, b) is rescaled per security by S^a · D^b , where S and D are the cumulative split and dividend factors between E′ and E . Most alpha factors have degree (0, 0) and need no rescale. A node without a degree ( log(close) ) is not served from the grid for a request that ends before E ; FactorDB falls back to the direct engine for it. When the panel publishes a new version FactorDB appends : for every node, the new dates are computed from the inputs over the new dates plus the node's look-back (the sum of its nested windows; unbounded recurrences such as ts_ema are recomputed in full). Securities with a new split or dividend have their whole column recomputed, because the new event changes their adjusted history. On a typical day that is a few dozen columns out of ~9,000. 3. Compute: column-sharded and parallel A batch of expressions becomes one DAG (shared subtrees appear once). Missing frontier nodes are computed by a pool of worker processes, each owning a slice of the security axis: the parent allocates the output year blocks as memory-mapped files; each worker maps the input fields (QFinVerse year blocks, already memory-mapped), evaluates every missing node of the batch for its columns with an in-worker CSE memo, and writes into its column slice of the outputs; nothing large crosses process boundaries; the OS page cache shares the inputs. Time-series kernels are independent per column, so this scales with cores until memory bandwidth runs out. Cross-sectional layers and scoring (IC, RankIC, decay, turnover) run per date in the parent, vectorised. Precision: inputs are float32; kernels compute in float64 within a worker; stored nodes are float32. Scores agree with the direct engine to well under 1e-4 in IC. 3.1 Spec packs (worker inputs) ADES workers score whole factors on one spec (universe, period). Every factor of a spec reads the same inputs: the OHLCV of every security that was a member during the period, aligned and adjusted onto the period's last day, the membership mask, and the forward returns per horizon. With ASSAY_PACK_DIR set ( /var/cache/assay-worker/packs on the workers), assay.data.specpack keeps them per panel snapshot as C-contiguous float64 .npy files and maps them read-only: TOP1000 2016+ (2723 × 2421) gathered from the panel spec pack load 5.4 s ~0 s (first build ~2 s on a worker) peak RSS scoring 55 Alpha101 factors 2.6 GB 1.5 GB disk — 460 MB Scores are identical bit for bit. A pack is built on first use (the directory and each forward-return file appear by rename), horizons are added as they are asked for, and a newer panel snapshot gets new packs while the older ones are removed. Processes on one machine share the mapped pages. 4. Agent-native interface Designed for many agents sharing one server: Principle How Batch first submit hundreds of expressions in one call; get a job id Idempotent factor id = canonical hash; a known factor on a known spec returns its stored score Shared across agents one node store and one registry; in-flight duplicates join the running job Small, stable payloads top-k tables with fixed keys; values only on request, sampled Actionable errors every rejection carries a code, the location in the expression and a hint Novelty built in correlation against the library computed from stored values Fair use per-owner job queue served round-robin, so one agent cannot starve the rest; an optional daily compute cap ( ASSAY_FACTORDB_BUDGET_S , off by default) Provenance every factor records who proposed it, when, from which parent factors, with tags 4.1 MCP tools (v2) Tool Purpose fdb_submit Evaluate many expressions on a spec (universe, period, horizons). Returns the job id plus immediate verdicts: duplicates, rejects with hints, already-scored factors fdb_job Progress, ETA, the best factors so far, failure summary fdb_query Search scored factors: filters on metrics, tags, owner, novelty; sort; limit fdb_factor One factor: canonical form, scores per spec, diagnostics, lineage fdb_novelty Max correlation of an expression or id against the library, with the nearest factors fdb_values A cross-section snapshot (top/bottom names and values on a date) to sanity-check a factor fdb_operators Operator catalog with signatures, categories and degree rules fdb_budget Compute used and left for the caller The MCP server is also served over streamable HTTP at /mcp on the Assay site, behind the same accounts and personal API keys as the REST API, so remote agents (Claude, Codex, …) connect to one shared FactorDB. 4.2 REST The same operations under /v1/fdb/* ( POST /submit , GET /jobs/{id} , GET /factors , GET /factors/{id} , POST /novelty , GET /values , GET /operators , GET /budget ). 5. Minute bars (phase 2) Minute data is two orders of magnitude larger (MASSIVE minute aggregates, ~100 GB of parquet for 2003–2026). The design reuses the same pieces with the trading day as the unit of parallelism instead of the security: a minute field store with one block per day ( 390 regular-session bars × members of the day ), float32, aligned to the daily grid's security ids; intraday expressions are evaluated per day (time axis = bar of the session), so days run in parallel with no cross-talk; the main use is intraday features reduced to daily values — day_agg(expr, "last" | "mean" | "sum" | "std" | …) — which land in the daily node store and combine freely with daily operators ( cs_rank(day_agg(ts_corr(close, volume, 30), "mean")) ); full minute-level outputs are stored per day only when a minute backtest asks for them. 6. Phases Daily FactorDB — canonical ids, global grid, node store, column-sharded parallel compute, append and corporate-action invalidation, registry and jobs, REST and MCP v2, HTTP MCP behind accounts. Benchmarked against the current engine. Minute bars — minute field store builder, per-day intraday evaluation, day_agg , minute backtests. Scale-out — eviction by cost × hits, node store on a shared volume for several compute hosts, scheduled precompute of the library's frontier after each panel update.

title: Assay — Full-Stack Architecture Design
headings: 2.1  What exists today — the engine entry point ✅
text: Assay — Full-Stack Architecture Design Version: 0.1 · Draft Scope: Functional API · REST API · WebUI · MCP for Agents Implementation status (2026-06). The entire Python backend is now implemented and tested (662 offline tests green): data layer, factor engine, the IC/RankIC/decay/groups/ turnover evaluator , the factor library (persistence + correlation + redundancy + prune), the AssayService singleton (evaluate / batch / sessions / streaming), the Python SDK ( assay.backtest/batch_backtest/Session/library/stream ), the REST API (FastAPI + SSE), the MCP server (8 FastMCP tools, stdio + SSE/HTTP), and the CLI ( run / batch / report / library / serve-api / serve-mcp ). See src/assay/ . Still planned : the React WebUI (§5, no assay-ui/ yet); and two performance optimizations the backend works correctly without — the L1 Arena / incremental O(1) cache (only a session cache + L2 disk cache exist today) and DAG/CSE batch merging ( batch() evaluates factors independently for now). Sections are tagged accordingly. Status legend — ✅ Implemented · 🔶 Implemented, simplified vs spec · 📋 Planned The single universe wired up end-to-end today is NASDAQ-100 (PIT constituent history from MASSIVE); SP500 / Russell 2000 are roadmap. The data source is MASSIVE US-equity day aggregates, which provide OHLCV + transaction count but no vwap . Table of Contents Architecture Overview Core Engine (Shared Backend) Functional Python API REST API WebUI Frontend MCP Server for Agents Cross-Cutting Concerns Deployment 1. Architecture Overview 1.1 Design philosophy Assay exposes four consumption surfaces over a single shared engine. Every surface calls the same underlying computation, cache, and data layer — there is no "API version" of a result vs a "SDK version". This means: A factor evaluated via Python SDK, REST API, WebUI, or MCP agent call produces an identical FactorReport Cache is shared across all surfaces — a REST call that warms the L1 operator cache benefits a subsequent SDK call Auth, rate limiting, and lineage tracking apply uniformly regardless of entry point 1.2 Layer diagram The dot on each box marks its build status: green for implemented, amber for partial, hollow for planned. Built today: the full stack except the React WebUI — DataStore , FactorEngine + dual-syntax parser + operators + diagnostics, the IC/decay/groups/turnover Evaluator , the FactorLibrary , the AssayService facade, and the SDK / REST / MCP / CLI surfaces. The cache is a session + L2-disk cache (the L1 Arena and incremental O(1) update layer remain a perf optimization), and batch() runs factors independently (DAG/CSE is future). 1.3 Surface comparison Latency targets remain design goals (no L1 cache / DAG-CSE yet), but all four code surfaces below except the WebUI are implemented and tested. Surface Protocol Auth Latency target Primary user Status Python SDK In-process None (local) < 400ms warm Researcher, notebook ✅ assay.backtest/batch_backtest/Session/library/stream REST API HTTP/SSE API key (optional) < 500ms warm External apps, CI ✅ FastAPI + SSE, all /v1/* routes WebUI HTTP → REST same-origin < 600ms warm Human researcher 🔶 zero-install vanilla-JS app ( api/static/ , served by FastAPI); React stack is the target rebuild MCP Server JSON-RPC (stdio/SSE) API key < 600ms warm LLM agent ✅ FastMCP, 11 tools, stdio + SSE 2. Core Engine (Shared Backend) Status: ✅ Implemented ( src/assay/service.py ). The AssayService singleton, sessions, streaming, and library wiring all exist. The sketch below matches the shipped API closely; the live constructor wires DataStore (lazily), FactorLibrary , the L2FactorCache , and a SessionRegistry . batch() is implemented via a thread pool (DAG/CSE merging is still a future optimization). See §2.1 for a minimal direct-engine path that bypasses the service. All four surfaces route through AssayService , which owns the engine, cache, and data access. It is never instantiated more than once per process. # assay/service.py ✅ IMPLEMENTED (sketch — see source for the exact signature) class AssayService: """ Singleton service. All surfaces call this. Thread-safe: uses a read-write lock on the factor library.
